translations.idiomatic: Ma Hao

sentences.zh: 何鑒，字世光，浙江新昌人。

translations.literal: He Jian, style name Shiguang, was a man of Xinchang in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He Jian, whose style name was Shiguang, was a native of Xinchang in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 成化五年進士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chenghua he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Chenghua reign he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 授宜興知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Yixing.

sentences.zh: 征拜御史，巡宣府、大同。

translations.literal: Summoned and appointed censor, he inspected Xuanfu and Datong.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to office as a censor, he toured Xuanfu and Datong.

sentences.zh: 劾巡撫鄭寧以下數十人不職，按裨將孟璽等罪。

translations.literal: He impeached Grand Coordinator Zheng Ning and dozens below him for dereliction, and investigated the crimes of deputy generals Meng Xi and others.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Grand Coordinator Zheng Ning and dozens of officials under him for neglect of duty, and prosecuted the offenses of deputy generals such as Meng Xi.

sentences.zh: 還巡太倉。

translations.literal: On returning he inspected Taicang.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he inspected Taicang.

sentences.zh: 總督太監卒犯法，逮治之，為所構，下錦衣獄。

translations.literal: Soldiers under the supervising eunuch broke the law; he arrested and prosecuted them, was framed by them, and was cast into the Brocade Guard prison.
translations.idiomatic: When soldiers under the grand coordinator's eunuch broke the law, he arrested and tried them; they framed him, and he was thrown into the Brocade Guard prison.

sentences.zh: 得釋，再按江北。

translations.literal: Released, he again conducted inspections in Jiangbei.
translations.idiomatic: After he was released, he again conducted inspections in the Jiangbei region.

sentences.zh: 鳳陽皇陵所在，近境取寸木，法皆死，陵軍多倚禁虐民。

translations.literal: Fengyang, where the imperial tombs stood: taking even a piece of wood from the vicinity was by law punishable by death, and the tomb guards often relied on the prohibition to abuse the people.
translations.idiomatic: Fengyang, where the imperial tombs lay, was nearby; under the law even taking a splinter of wood from the vicinity meant death, and the tomb guards often abused the people under cover of the prohibition.

sentences.zh: 鑒請以山麓為限，他樵采勿禁，遂著為令。

translations.literal: He Jian requested that the mountain foothills be set as the limit and that wood-gathering elsewhere not be forbidden; this was then established as an ordinance.
translations.idiomatic: He Jian asked that the mountain foothills be set as the boundary and that gathering firewood elsewhere be permitted; this was then written into law.

sentences.zh: 出為河南知府。

translations.literal: He left office to become prefect of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to become prefect of Henan.

sentences.zh: 振累歲饑，條行荒政十事。

translations.literal: After successive years of famine he drew up ten measures for famine administration.
translations.idiomatic: After years of famine he drew up ten measures for famine relief.

sentences.zh: 歷四川左、右布政使。

translations.literal: He served successively as left and right administrative commissioner of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as left and right administrative commissioner of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 弘治六年以右副都御史巡撫江南，兼理杭、嘉、湖三府稅糧。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Hongzhi he was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Jiangnan, with concurrent charge of the grain tax of Hangzhou, Jiaxing, and Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Hongzhi he was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Jiangnan, with charge also of the grain tax of Hangzhou, Jiaxing, and Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 蘇、松水災，用便宜發漕米十五萬石振之。

translations.literal: When Suzhou and Songjiang suffered flood damage, he used his discretionary authority to release 150,000 piculs of transported grain for relief.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzhou and Songjiang suffered flooding, he used his discretionary authority to release 150,000 piculs of transported grain for relief.

sentences.zh: 與侍郎徐貫疏吳淞、白茆諸渠，泄水入海，水患以除。

translations.literal: Together with Vice Minister Xu Guan he memorialized on dredging the channels of the Wusong River, the Baimao River, and others, draining the water into the sea, and the water calamities were thereby removed.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Vice Minister Xu Guan he memorialized on dredging the Wusong, Baimao, and other channels so the water could drain to the sea, and the flood disasters were thereby ended.

sentences.zh: 復巡撫山東，遷刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: He again served as grand coordinator of Shandong and was promoted to Vice Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as grand coordinator of Shandong and was promoted to Vice Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 母憂去。

translations.literal: He left office on account of his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 十八年還朝。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he returned to court.

sentences.zh: 時承平久，生齒日繁。

translations.literal: The realm had long been at peace and the population grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: The realm had long been at peace, and the population grew day by day.

sentences.zh: 孝宗覽天下戶籍數乃視國初反減，咎所司溺職，欲厘正之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozong reviewed the empire's household registers and found the numbers had actually fallen since the founding of the dynasty; he blamed the responsible offices for negligence and wished to rectify the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozong reviewed the empire's household registers and found the numbers had actually fallen since the founding of the dynasty; he blamed the responsible offices for negligence and wished to set the matter right.

sentences.zh: 敕鑒以故官兼左僉都御史往河南、湖廣、陜西閱實戶口。

translations.literal: He ordered He Jian, in his former rank supplemented by Left Censor-in-Chief, to proceed to Henan, Huguang, and Shaanxi to verify household registers.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered He Jian, retaining his former rank while also serving as Left Censor-in-Chief, to go to Henan, Huguang, and Shaanxi to verify household registers.

sentences.zh: 得戶二十三萬五千有奇，口七十三萬九千有奇，因疏善後十事及軍民利病以聞。

translations.literal: He registered 235,000-odd households and 739,000-odd persons, and memorialized ten measures for follow-up administration and the advantages and harms affecting soldiers and civilians.
translations.idiomatic: He registered more than 235,000 households and more than 739,000 persons, and memorialized ten follow-up measures together with the advantages and harms affecting soldiers and civilians.

sentences.zh: 會孝宗已崩，武宗悉采納之。

translations.literal: By then Emperor Xiaozong had died, but Emperor Wuzong adopted all of his recommendations.
translations.idiomatic: By then Emperor Xiaozong had died, but Emperor Wuzong adopted all of his recommendations.

sentences.zh: 正德二年拜南京兵部尚書參贊機務。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengde he was appointed Minister of War at Nanjing with concurrent participation in deliberations on state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhengde he was appointed Minister of War at Nanjing with concurrent participation in state deliberations.

sentences.zh: 鑒前撫江南，嘗按千戶張文冕罪，文冕亡去。

translations.literal: When He Jian had earlier administered Jiangnan, he had prosecuted the offense of battalion commander Zhang Wenmian, who had fled.
translations.idiomatic: When He Jian had earlier served as grand coordinator of Jiangnan, he had prosecuted the battalion commander Zhang Wenmian for an offense; Zhang fled.

sentences.zh: 至是構於劉瑾，而瑾亦嗛鑒不與通，遂坐以事連罰米。

translations.literal: Now Zhang framed him before Liu Jin, and Jin also resented He Jian for refusing contact; he was therefore punished by being ordered to provide rice.
translations.idiomatic: Now Zhang framed him before Liu Jin, and Jin also resented He Jian for refusing to deal with him; he was therefore punished by being ordered to provide rice as a fine.

sentences.zh: 貧不能償，奏訴獲免。

translations.literal: Unable to pay because he was poor, he submitted a petition and was excused.
translations.idiomatic: Too poor to pay, he submitted a petition and was excused.

sentences.zh: 六年正月，召為刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixth year he was summoned to be Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the sixth year he was summoned to serve as Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 時大盜並起，劉寵、劉宸、楊虎、劉惠、齊彥名、朱諒等亂畿輔；

translations.literal: At that time great bandits rose everywhere; Liu Chong, Liu Chen, Yang Hu, Liu Hui, Qi Yanming, Zhu Liang, and others threw the capital region into turmoil;
translations.idiomatic: At that time great bandits rose everywhere: Liu Chong, Liu Chen, Yang Hu, Liu Hui, Qi Yanming, Zhu Liang, and others threw the capital region into turmoil;

sentences.zh: 方四、曹甫、藍廷瑞、鄢本恕等躪四川；

translations.literal: Fang Si, Cao Fu, Lan Tingrui, Yan Benshu, and others trampled Sichuan;
translations.idiomatic: Fang Si, Cao Fu, Lan Tingrui, Yan Benshu, and others overran Sichuan;

sentences.zh: 汪澄二、羅光權、王浩八、王鈺五等擾江西，皆稱王。

translations.literal: Wang Cheng'er, Luo Guangquan, Wang Haoba, Wang Yuwu, and others harassed Jiangxi—all styling themselves kings.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Cheng'er, Luo Guangquan, Wang Haoba, Wang Yuwu, and others harassed Jiangxi—all proclaiming themselves kings.

sentences.zh: 四方告急無虛日。

translations.literal: Distress reports from every quarter came in day after day without pause.
translations.idiomatic: Distress reports from every quarter arrived day after day without letup.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書王敞不能辦賊。

translations.literal: Minister of War Wang Chang could not deal with the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Wang Chang could not deal with the bandits.

sentences.zh: 帝既命洪鐘、陳金、馬中錫督師分討。

translations.literal: The Emperor had already ordered Hong Zhong, Chen Jin, and Ma Zhongxi to command armies and pursue them separately.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had already ordered Hong Zhong, Chen Jin, and Ma Zhongxi to take command of armies and pursue the bandits separately.

sentences.zh: 其年五月，罷敞，以鑒代之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of that year Chang was removed and He Jian replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of that year Chang was dismissed and He Jian replaced him.

sentences.zh: 鑒乃選將練兵，錄民間材武士，令鄉聚悉樹柵浚溝，團結相救。

translations.literal: He Jian thereupon selected generals and trained troops, enrolled able-bodied martial men from among the populace, and ordered every village to erect stockades, dig ditches, and unite for mutual rescue.
translations.idiomatic: He Jian thereupon selected generals and trained troops, enrolled able-bodied martial men from among the people, and ordered every village to erect stockades, dig ditches, and unite for mutual defense.

sentences.zh: 河南、山西兵守黃河，斷太行。

translations.literal: Troops from Henan and Shanxi guarded the Yellow River and blocked the Taihang passes.
translations.idiomatic: Troops from Henan and Shanxi guarded the Yellow River and blocked the Taihang passes.

sentences.zh: 京操班軍，留守所在城邑。

translations.literal: Capital drill troops and rotation troops remained to garrison the cities of their stations.
translations.idiomatic: Capital drill troops and rotation troops remained to garrison the cities where they were stationed.

sentences.zh: 每漕艘運卒一人屯河濱，護運道，通行旅。

translations.literal: For each grain transport vessel one transport soldier was stationed along the riverbank to guard the transport route and keep travelers safe.
translations.idiomatic: For each grain transport vessel one transport soldier was stationed along the riverbank to guard the transport route and keep travelers safe.

sentences.zh: 文武大吏軼賊，請敕峻責之，而褒縣令能擊賊者。

translations.literal: When civil and military officials high and low missed the bandits, he requested stern imperial reprimand, while rewarding magistrates who could strike down bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When civil and military officials of every rank let the bandits slip away, he asked that the throne issue stern reprimands, while rewarding magistrates who could defeat bandits.

sentences.zh: 以中錫玩寇，奏遣陸完代還，調邊將從完討賊。

translations.literal: Because Ma Zhongxi had treated the bandits lightly, he memorialized to send Lu Wan in his place and to transfer frontier generals to follow Wan in hunting the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Because Ma Zhongxi had treated the bandits lightly, he memorialized to send Lu Wan to replace him and to transfer frontier generals to follow Wan in hunting the bandits.

sentences.zh: 賊連為邊軍所破，奔迸四出。

translations.literal: The bandits, repeatedly broken by frontier troops, fled in all directions.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits, repeatedly broken by frontier troops, fled in all directions.

sentences.zh: 會中官谷大用、伏羌伯毛銳率師駐臨清，賊遂謀以十二月朔伺帝省牲南郊，乘間犯駕，先一日趨霸州。

translations.literal: When the eunuch Gu Dayong and the hereditary noble Fuqiang Bo Mao Rui led troops stationed at Linqing, the bandits resolved that on the first day of the twelfth month, when the Emperor would inspect the sacrificial animals at the Southern Suburb, they would seize the opportunity to assault the imperial procession; they therefore advanced one day earlier toward Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the eunuch Gu Dayong and the hereditary noble Fuqiang Bo Mao Rui led troops stationed at Linqing, the bandits resolved that on the first day of the twelfth month, when the Emperor would inspect the sacrificial animals at the Southern Suburb, they would seize the opportunity to assault the imperial procession; they therefore advanced one day early toward Bazhou.

sentences.zh: 鑒立奏聞，夜設備。

translations.literal: He Jian immediately memorialized the Emperor and made preparations through the night.
translations.idiomatic: He Jian immediately memorialized the Emperor and made preparations through the night.

sentences.zh: 厥明，帝召問鑒。

translations.literal: At dawn the Emperor summoned him for questioning.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the Emperor summoned He Jian for questioning.

sentences.zh: 鑒請早出安人心，遂成禮而還。

translations.literal: He Jian asked that the Emperor set out early to reassure people's hearts; the rites were completed and he returned.
translations.idiomatic: He Jian asked that the Emperor set out early to reassure the people; the rites were completed and he returned.

sentences.zh: 賊知有備，西掠保定諸州縣以去。

translations.literal: Learning there were preparations, the bandits raided westward through Baoding and other prefectures and counties before departing.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that preparations had been made, the bandits raided west through Baoding and other prefectures and counties before departing.

sentences.zh: 河南巡撫鄧璋請濟師，鑒言：「山東賊不及萬，官軍奚啻十倍。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Deng Zhang of Henan requested reinforcements; He Jian said: "The bandits in Shandong number fewer than ten thousand, while government troops are more than ten times that many."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Deng Zhang of Henan requested reinforcements; He Jian said, "The bandits in Shandong number fewer than ten thousand, while government troops are more than ten times as many."

sentences.zh: 緣勢要私人營充頭目，撓律攘功，失將士心。

translations.literal: "Because powerful men's private dependents have been installed as commanders, they obstruct discipline and seize credit, and the officers and soldiers have lost heart."
translations.idiomatic: "Because private dependents of the powerful have been installed as commanders, they obstruct discipline and seize credit, and the officers and soldiers have lost heart."

sentences.zh: 請盡遣若屬還。

translations.literal: "I ask that all such persons be sent back."
translations.idiomatic: "I ask that all such persons be sent back."

sentences.zh: 都指揮以下失事，即軍前行戮。

translations.literal: "Any regional commander or below who fails in action shall be executed on the spot before the army."
translations.idiomatic: "Any regional commander or below who fails in action shall be executed on the spot before the army."

sentences.zh: 益調邊軍助璋。

translations.literal: "Further dispatch frontier troops to aid Zhang."
translations.idiomatic: "Further dispatch frontier troops to aid Zhang."

sentences.zh: 」帝悉從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor adopted all of this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor adopted all of this.

sentences.zh: 尋以捷書屢聞，加鑒太子少保。

translations.literal: Soon reports of victory arrived repeatedly, and He Jian was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon reports of victory arrived repeatedly, and He Jian was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，賊突霸州，京師戒嚴。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year the bandits suddenly attacked Bazhou and the capital went on alert.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year the bandits suddenly attacked Bazhou, and the capital went on alert.

sentences.zh: 鑒令邊兵亟邀賊，賊遁去。

translations.literal: He Jian ordered frontier troops to intercept the bandits quickly, and they fled.
translations.idiomatic: He Jian ordered frontier troops to intercept the bandits at once, and they fled.

sentences.zh: 賊渠楊虎、朱諒死，其黨分擾山東、河南。

translations.literal: The bandit chiefs Yang Hu and Zhu Liang died, and their bands dispersed to harass Shandong and Henan separately.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit chiefs Yang Hu and Zhu Liang died, and their followers dispersed to harass Shandong and Henan separately.

sentences.zh: 鑒以山東賊劉寵、劉宸、齊彥名等，責邊將許泰、郤永、劉暉、李鋐；

translations.literal: For the Shandong bandits Liu Chong, Liu Chen, Qi Yanming, and others, He Jian held frontier generals Xu Tai, Xi Yong, Liu Hui, and Li Zhen responsible;
translations.idiomatic: For the Shandong bandits Liu Chong, Liu Chen, Qi Yanming, and others, he held frontier generals Xu Tai, Xi Yong, Liu Hui, and Li Zhen responsible;

sentences.zh: 以河南賊劉惠、趙鐩、刑老虎等，責邊將馮禎、時源、神周、金輔。

translations.literal: for the Henan bandits Liu Hui, Zhao Zan, Xing Laohu, and others, he held frontier generals Feng Zhen, Shi Yuan, Shen Zhou, and Jin Fu responsible.
translations.idiomatic: for the Henan bandits Liu Hui, Zhao Zan, Xing Laohu, and others, he held frontier generals Feng Zhen, Shi Yuan, Shen Zhou, and Jin Fu responsible.

sentences.zh: 未幾，毛銳敗績，與大用俱召還。

translations.literal: Before long Mao Rui suffered defeat and he and Dayong were both recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Mao Rui suffered defeat, and he and Dayong were both recalled.

sentences.zh: 鑒乃請用彭澤，與仇鉞同辦河南賊，而以山東賊專委陸完。

translations.literal: He Jian then requested the employment of Peng Ze, who with Qiu Yao would together handle the Henan bandits, while entrusting the Shandong bandits solely to Lu Wan.
translations.idiomatic: He Jian then requested that Peng Ze be employed, who together with Qiu Yao would handle the Henan bandits, while the Shandong bandits were entrusted solely to Lu Wan.

sentences.zh: 五月，河南賊平。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the Henan bandits were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the Henan bandits were pacified.

sentences.zh: 七月，山東余賊亦平。

translations.literal: In the seventh month the remaining bandits in Shandong were also pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the remaining bandits in Shandong were also pacified.

sentences.zh: 陳金、洪鐘亦以次平江西、四川諸賊。

translations.literal: Chen Jin and Hong Zhong likewise pacified the bandits of Jiangxi and Sichuan in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jin and Hong Zhong likewise pacified the bandits of Jiangxi and Sichuan in turn.

sentences.zh: 帝喜，加鑒太子太保，蔭子錦衣世百戶。

translations.literal: The Emperor rejoiced, made He Jian Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and conferred hereditary enrollment in the Embroidered Guard on his son for one hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor rejoiced, made He Jian Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and conferred hereditary enrollment in the Embroidered Guard on his son for one hundred households.

sentences.zh: 鑒乃上言：「群盜蕩平，民罹兵久，乞量免田租，多方振贍。

translations.literal: He Jian then memorialized: "The massed bandits have been swept away; the people have long suffered from warfare—I beg that land tax be remitted in measure and relief be provided by every means."
translations.idiomatic: He Jian then memorialized, "The massed bandits have been swept away; the people have long suffered from warfare—I beg that land tax be remitted in measure and relief be provided by every means."

sentences.zh: 黜貪殘長吏，停不急工役。

translations.literal: "Remove corrupt and cruel senior officials; halt unurgent labor corvée."
translations.idiomatic: "Remove corrupt and cruel senior officials; halt unurgent labor corvée."

sentences.zh: 還民故業，貸以牛種，復其家三年。

translations.literal: "Restore the people to their former livelihoods, lend them oxen and seed, and exempt their households for three years."
translations.idiomatic: "Restore the people to their former livelihoods, lend them oxen and seed, and exempt their households for three years."

sentences.zh: 有訐舊事及怙惡者，並置於理。

translations.literal: "Those who impeach on old scores or cling to evil shall all be brought to justice."
translations.idiomatic: "Those who bring up old grievances or cling to evil shall all be brought to justice."

sentences.zh: 」帝悉報可。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved all of this in reply.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved all of this in reply.

sentences.zh: 先是，七月中，鑒以群盜未盡，請留邊將劉暉戍山東，時源戍河南，郤永戍畿輔，李鋐戍淮、揚，各假總兵之職，俟事寧始罷。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the seventh month He Jian, because the massed bandits were not yet fully gone, had asked that frontier general Liu Hui be left to garrison Shandong, Shi Yuan Henan, Xi Yong the capital region, and Li Zhen Huaiyang, each given acting powers of regional commander until affairs were settled.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the seventh month, because the massed bandits were not yet fully gone, He Jian had asked that frontier general Liu Hui garrison Shandong, Shi Yuan Henan, Xi Yong the capital region, and Li Zhen Huaiyang, each given acting powers of regional commander until affairs were settled.

sentences.zh: 仇鉞言，邊軍久勞，風土不習，人馬俱病。

translations.literal: Qiu Yao said the frontier armies had labored long, were unaccustomed to the climate and terrain, and both men and horses were worn out.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Yao said the frontier armies had labored long, were unaccustomed to the climate and terrain, and both men and horses were worn out.

sentences.zh: 今賊已漸平，請留三之一討賊，余悉遣還。

translations.literal: "Now that the bandits are gradually pacified, I ask that one-third be kept to pursue bandits and the rest all sent back."
translations.idiomatic: "Now that the bandits are gradually being pacified, I ask that one-third be kept to pursue bandits and the rest all sent back."

sentences.zh: 廷議，二人議俱是，請四將各千人鎮壓，他將許泰、神周、金輔、溫恭輩俱統所部還邊鎮。

translations.literal: At court it was debated; both men's views were held correct, and it was requested that each of the four generals keep one thousand men for suppression while the other generals—Xu Tai, Shen Zhou, Jin Fu, Wen Gong, and the rest—should each lead their commands back to frontier garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: At court it was debated; both views were held correct, and it was requested that each of the four generals keep one thousand men for suppression while the other generals—Xu Tai, Shen Zhou, Jin Fu, Wen Gong, and the rest—should each lead their commands back to frontier garrisons.

sentences.zh: 帝許之，命延綏軍徑還，遼東、宣府，大同軍過闕勞賜。

translations.literal: The Emperor consented, ordering the Yan-sui army to return directly and the Liaodong, Xuanfu, and Datong armies to pass through the capital for labor and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor consented, ordering the Yan-sui army to return directly and the Liaodong, Xuanfu, and Datong armies to pass through the capital for commendation and rewards.

sentences.zh: 帝時好弄兵。

translations.literal: The Emperor at this time delighted in military exercises.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor at this time delighted in military exercises.

sentences.zh: 群小寵幸者言邊軍憨健過京軍遠甚，宜留之京營。

translations.literal: Favorites among his entourage said frontier troops were far sturdier and readier than capital troops and ought to be kept in the capital camps.
translations.idiomatic: Favorites among his entourage said frontier troops were far sturdier and readier than capital troops and ought to be kept in the capital camps.

sentences.zh: 帝以為然。

translations.literal: The Emperor thought this correct.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor thought this correct.

sentences.zh: 至十一月，三鎮軍畢至，遂命留之，以京軍往代。

translations.literal: By the eleventh month the armies of the three garrisons had all arrived, and he ordered them kept while capital troops went to replace them on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: By the eleventh month the armies of the three garrisons had all arrived, and he ordered them kept while capital troops went to replace them on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 鑒力陳不可，廷臣集議，復極言其害，帝竟不從。

translations.literal: He Jian urged forcefully that this could not be done; court officials assembled for deliberation and again spoke at length of the harm, yet the Emperor in the end would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: He Jian urged forcefully that this could not be done; court officials assembled for deliberation and again spoke at length of the harm, yet the Emperor in the end would not agree.

sentences.zh: 自是，邊軍於大內團操，號為「外四家軍」，而江彬進用矣。

translations.literal: From this time frontier troops drilled in formation within the inner palace, styled the "Four Outer Garrison Armies," and Jiang Bin came into employment.
translations.idiomatic: From this time frontier troops drilled in formation within the inner palace, styled the "Four Outer Garrison Armies," and Jiang Bin came into favor.

sentences.zh: 八年，宣府送迤北降人脫脫太等至京，命充禦馬監勇士。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Xuanfu sent surrendered men from the northern frontier, Tuotuotai and others, to the capital, and the Emperor ordered them enrolled as warriors of the Imperial Stud Service.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Xuanfu sent surrendered men from the northern frontier, Tuotuotai and others, to the capital, and the Emperor ordered them enrolled as warriors of the Imperial Stud Service.

sentences.zh: 鑒等上言：「漢、魏徙氐、羌於關中，郭欽、江統皆勸晉武早絕亂階。

translations.literal: He Jian and others memorialized: "In Han and Wei the Di and Qiang were moved into the Guanzhong region; Guo Qin and Jiang Tong both urged Emperor Wu of Jin to cut off the source of disorder early."
translations.idiomatic: He Jian and others memorialized, "In Han and Wei the Di and Qiang were moved into the Guanzhong region; Guo Qin and Jiang Tong both urged Emperor Wu of Jin to cut off the source of disorder early."

sentences.zh: 苻堅處鮮卑於漢南，苻融亦慮其窺測虛實。

translations.literal: "Fu Jian settled the Xianbei south of the Han River, and Fu Rong also feared they would spy out weakness."
translations.idiomatic: "Fu Jian settled the Xianbei south of the Han River, and Fu Rong also feared they would spy out the court's weaknesses."

sentences.zh: 今使降人出入禁中，假寵逾分，且生慢侮。

translations.literal: "Now to let surrendered men enter and leave the forbidden palace, granting them favor beyond their station, will moreover breed contempt and disrespect."
translations.idiomatic: "Now to let surrendered men enter and leave the forbidden palace, granting them favor beyond their station, will moreover breed contempt and disrespect."

sentences.zh: 萬一北寇聞之，潛使黠賊偽降，以為間諜，寧不為將來患哉？

translations.literal: "Should northern invaders hear of this and secretly send cunning bandits to feign surrender as spies, will this not become a calamity for the future?"
translations.idiomatic: "Should northern invaders hear of this and secretly send cunning men to feign surrender as spies, will this not become a calamity for the future?"

sentences.zh: 」帝不聽。

translations.literal: The Emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 寧王宸濠謀復護衛，鑒力遏之。

translations.literal: Prince of Ning Zhu Chenhao plotted to recover his guard forces; He Jian barred the way firmly.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Ning, Zhu Chenhao, plotted to recover his guard forces; He Jian firmly barred the way.

sentences.zh: 都督白玉以失事罷，厚賄豹房諸幸臣求復，鑒執不從。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Bai Yu, dismissed for failure, lavished bribes on the favored men of the leopard quarters to seek reinstatement; He Jian held firm and would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Bai Yu, dismissed for failure, lavished bribes on the favored men of the leopard quarters to seek reinstatement; He Jian held firm and would not agree.

sentences.zh: 諸幸臣嗾诇事者發鑒家僮取將校金錢，言官遂交章劾鑒，致仕去。

translations.literal: The favored men incited informers to expose He Jian's household servants taking money from commanders; censorial officials then submitted memorials in succession impeaching He Jian, and he left office and retired.
translations.idiomatic: The favored men incited informers to expose He Jian's household servants taking money from commanders; censorial officials then submitted memorials in succession impeaching He Jian, and he left office and retired.

sentences.zh: 閱九年卒，年八十。

translations.literal: Nine years later he died, aged eighty.
translations.idiomatic: Nine years later he died, aged eighty.

sentences.zh: 馬中錫，字天祿，故城人。

translations.literal: Ma Zhongxi, style name Tianlu, was a man of Gucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zhongxi, whose style name was Tianlu, was a native of Gucheng.

sentences.zh: 父偉，為唐府長史，以直諫忤王，械送京師，而盡縲其家人。

translations.literal: His father Wei served as secretary of the Tang princely establishment; for a straight remonstrance that offended the prince, he was shackled and sent to the capital, and his entire household was bound and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wei served as secretary of the Tang princely establishment; after a forthright remonstrance offended the prince, he was shackled and sent to the capital while the entire family was thrown into chains.

sentences.zh: 中錫以幼免，乃奔訴巡按御史。

translations.literal: Zhongxi, because he was young, was spared; he then fled to plead his case before the touring censor.
translations.idiomatic: Spared on account of his youth, Zhongxi fled to appeal to the touring censor.

sentences.zh: 御史言於王，釋其家。

translations.literal: The censor spoke to the prince, and his family was released.
translations.idiomatic: The censor appealed to the prince, and the family was freed.

sentences.zh: 復奉母走京師訴冤，父竟得白，終處州知府。

translations.literal: He again took his mother and hurried to the capital to plead his father's wrong; his father was ultimately cleared and finished his career as prefect of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Taking his mother, he rushed to the capital to seek redress; his father was ultimately exonerated and ended his career as prefect of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 中錫舉成化十年鄉試第一，明年成進士，授刑科給事中。

translations.literal: Zhongxi placed first in the provincial examination of the tenth year of Chenghua; the next year he passed the metropolitan examination and was appointed supervising secretary in the Bureau of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxi topped the provincial examinations in Chenghua 10; the following year he became a metropolitan graduate and was appointed supervising secretary in the Bureau of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 萬貴妃弟通驕橫，再疏斥之，再被杖。

translations.literal: Tong, younger brother of Consort Wan, was arrogant and overbearing; twice he memorialized against him and twice was beaten by the staff.
translations.idiomatic: Tong, younger brother of Consort Wan, was insufferably arrogant; Zhongxi denounced him twice in memorials and twice was beaten with the staff.

sentences.zh: 公主侵畿內田，勘還之民。

translations.literal: When a princess encroached on fields within the capital district, he surveyed and returned them to the people.
translations.idiomatic: When a princess seized lands within the capital region, he surveyed the holdings and restored them to the commoners.

sentences.zh: 又嘗劾汪直違恣罪。

translations.literal: He also once impeached Wang Zhi for wanton violations.
translations.idiomatic: He also impeached Wang Zhi on charges of lawless arrogance.

sentences.zh: 歷陜西督學副使。

translations.literal: He served in succession as vice commissioner for education in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as vice commissioner for education in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 弘治五年，召為大理右少卿。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Hongzhi he was summoned as Right Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 5 he was summoned to serve as Right Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 南京守備太監蔣琮與兵部郎中婁性、指揮石文通相訐，連數百人，遣官按，不服。

translations.literal: Nanjing garrison eunuch Jiang Cong and Bureau of War director Lou Xing and commander Shi Wentong sued one another; several hundred persons were implicated; officials were dispatched to investigate, but they would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: The Nanjing garrison eunuch Jiang Cong, Bureau of War director Lou Xing, and commander Shi Wentong had lodged mutual accusations implicating several hundred people; when investigators were sent, they refused to yield.

sentences.zh: 中錫偕司禮太監趙忠等往，一訊得實。

translations.literal: Zhongxi went together with Director of Ceremonials eunuch Zhao Zhong and others; a single inquiry established the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxi went with Zhao Zhong, Director of Ceremonials, and others; one round of questioning settled the matter.

sentences.zh: 性除名，琮下獄抵罪。

translations.literal: Xing was struck from the rolls; Cong was imprisoned to atone for his crime.
translations.idiomatic: Xing was struck from the rolls, and Cong was cast into prison to answer for his crimes.

sentences.zh: 擢右副都御史，巡撫宣府。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and commissioned as grand coordinator of Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, he was appointed grand coordinator of Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 劾罷貪耄總兵官馬儀，革鎮守以下私役軍士，使隸尺籍。

translations.literal: He impeached and removed the covetous, aged regional commander Ma Yi, abolished private impressment of soldiers by the garrison command and below, and had them entered on the roster rolls.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached and dismissed the grasping, aged regional commander Ma Yi, ended the private impressment of troops by the garrison command downward, and restored soldiers to the official muster rolls.

sentences.zh: 寇嘗犯邊，督軍敗之。

translations.literal: When raiders once invaded the border, he supervised the army and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders crossed the border, he directed the troops and repelled them.

sentences.zh: 引疾歸，中外交薦。

translations.literal: He cited illness and returned home; inside and outside the court he was widely recommended.
translations.idiomatic: He retired citing illness, and recommendations poured in from within and beyond the court.

sentences.zh: 武宗即位，起撫遼東。

translations.literal: When the Wuzong Emperor acceded, he was recalled to grand coordinator of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong took the throne, Zhongxi was recalled to serve as grand coordinator of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 還屯田於軍，而劾鎮守太監朱秀置官店、擅馬市諸罪。

translations.literal: He restored military colonies to the troops, and impeached garrison eunuch Zhu Xiu for establishing government shops, monopolizing horse markets, and other crimes.
translations.idiomatic: He restored colony lands to the troops and impeached the garrison eunuch Zhu Xiu for operating government shops, running private horse markets, and related offenses.

sentences.zh: 正德元年入歷兵部左右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengde he entered the Ministry of War as Left and Right Vice Minister in succession.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde 1 he advanced through the Ministry of War as Left and Right Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾初得誌，其黨朱瀛冒邊功至數百人。

translations.literal: When Liu Jin first had his way, his partisan Zhu Ying falsely claimed frontier merit for several hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Once Liu Jin held power, his follower Zhu Ying falsely claimed frontier merit for hundreds of men.

sentences.zh: 尚書閻仲宇許之，中錫持不可。

translations.literal: Minister Yan Zhongyu assented; Zhongxi insisted that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Yan Zhongyu agreed, but Zhongxi refused to allow it.

sentences.zh: 瑾大恚，中旨改南京工部。

translations.literal: Jin was greatly enraged; an edict from the center reassigned him to the Nanjing Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was furious; by secret edict Zhongxi was transferred to the Nanjing Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 明年勒致仕。

translations.literal: The next year he was compelled to retire.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was forced into retirement.

sentences.zh: 其冬，逮系詔獄，械送遼東，責償所收腐粟。

translations.literal: That winter he was seized and imprisoned in the Imperial Prison, shackled and sent to Liaodong, and ordered to repay the spoiled grain he had taken.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was seized and held in the Imperial Prison, then shackled and sent to Liaodong to repay the spoiled grain he had collected.

sentences.zh: 逾年事竣，斥為民。

translations.literal: After more than a year the affair was closed and he was reduced to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter closed a year later, he was demoted to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，起撫大同。

translations.literal: After Jin was executed, he was raised again as grand coordinator of Datong.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin's execution he was restored as grand coordinator of Datong.

sentences.zh: 中錫居官廉，所至革弊任怨，以故有名。

translations.literal: Zhongxi was incorrupt in office; wherever he went he reformed abuses and bore resentment, and so won a reputation.
translations.idiomatic: A scrupulously honest official, he reformed abuses wherever he served and willingly bore ill will—which is why his name endured.

sentences.zh: 六年三月，賊劉六等起，吏部尚書楊一清建議遣大臣節制諸道兵。

translations.literal: In the third month of the sixth year, the bandit Liu Six and others rose; Minister of Personnel Yang Yiqing proposed dispatching a grand minister to coordinate troops on every circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year six the bandits Liu Six and others rose; Minister of Personnel Yang Yiqing proposed sending a senior minister to coordinate forces on every circuit.

sentences.zh: 乃薦中錫為右都御史提督軍務，與惠安伯張偉統禁兵南征。

translations.literal: He thereupon recommended Zhongxi as Right Censor-in-Chief to supervise military affairs, together with Hui'an Earl Zhang Wei to command the capital guard army on a southern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Zhongxi as Right Censor-in-Chief to supervise military affairs, with Hui'an Earl Zhang Wei commanding the capital guard on a southern expedition.

sentences.zh: 劉六名寵，其弟七名宸，文安人也，並驍悍善騎射。

translations.literal: Liu Six's given name was Chong, his younger brother Seven's given name was Chen; they were men of Wen'an, both fierce and skilled at mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Six was really Liu Chong; his younger brother Liu Seven was Liu Chen. Both were from Wen'an—fierce men skilled in mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 先是，有司患盜，召寵、宸及其黨楊虎、齊彥名等協捕，頻有功。

translations.literal: Earlier, officials troubled by bandits had recruited Chong, Chen, and their followers Yang Hu and Qi Yanming to help capture bandits, and they had repeatedly won merit.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, harried by bandits, local officials had enlisted Chong, Chen, and their followers Yang Hu and Qi Yanming to assist in arrests; they had repeatedly distinguished themselves.

sentences.zh: 會劉瑾家人梁洪征賄於寵等不得，誣為盜。

translations.literal: But when Liu Jin's household retainer Liang Hong came to extort bribes from Chong and could not get them, he falsely accused them of banditry.
translations.idiomatic: Then Liu Jin's retainer Liang Hong tried to extort bribes from Chong and, rebuffed, denounced them as bandits.

sentences.zh: 遣寧杲、柳尚義繪形捕之，破其家。

translations.literal: Ning Gao and Liu Shangyi were sent to paint their likenesses for capture, and their families were ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Ning Gao and Liu Shangyi were sent to circulate wanted portraits; their families were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 寵等乃投大盜張茂。

translations.literal: Chong and the others then joined the great bandit Zhang Mao.
translations.idiomatic: Chong and his band threw in with the great outlaw Zhang Mao.

sentences.zh: 茂家高樓重屋，復壁深窖，素招亡命為逋逃主。

translations.literal: Mao's house had lofty towers and layered halls, double walls and deep vaults; he had long recruited fugitives as refuge.
translations.idiomatic: Mao lived in a fortress of towers and layered halls, with double walls and deep cellars, long sheltering fugitives as a haven.

sentences.zh: 宦官張忠與鄰，茂結為兄，夤緣馬永成、谷大用、於經輩得出入豹房，侍帝蹴鞠，而乘間為盜如故。

translations.literal: Eunuch Zhang Zhong was his neighbor; Mao bonded with him as brother, and through Ma Yongcheng, Gu Dayong, Yu Jing, and the like gained access to the Leopard Quarters to attend the Emperor at kickball—yet in spare moments he plundered as before.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Zhang Zhong lived next door; Mao treated him as a sworn brother and, courting Ma Yongcheng, Gu Dayong, Yu Jing, and their circle, won entry to the Leopard Quarters to attend the Emperor at kickball—yet stole whenever chance allowed.

sentences.zh: 後數為河間參將袁彪所敗。

translations.literal: Later he was several times defeated by Hejian assistant regional commander Yuan Biao.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Biao, assistant regional commander of Hejian, defeated him repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 茂窘，求救於忠。

translations.literal: Mao was cornered and begged Zhong for rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, Mao begged Zhong to save him.

sentences.zh: 忠置酒私第，招茂、彪東西坐。

translations.literal: Zhong set out wine in his private residence and seated Mao and Biao east and west.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong held a banquet at his private house and seated Mao and Biao facing each other.

sentences.zh: 酒酣，舉觴屬彪字茂曰：「彥實吾弟也，自今毋相厄。

translations.literal: When the wine was deep he raised a cup toward Biao and, naming Mao, said: "Yanshi is my younger brother; from this day do not harry one another.
translations.idiomatic: Deep in wine, he raised his cup to Biao and, turning to Mao, said, "Yanshi is my younger brother—from today onward, cease your persecution.

sentences.zh: 」又舉觴屬茂曰：「袁公善爾，爾慎毋犯河間。

translations.literal: " He again raised a cup toward Mao and said: "Lord Yuan favors you; take care not to invade Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: " He lifted another cup to Mao: "Lord Yuan is kindly disposed toward you—see that you do not raid Hejian.

sentences.zh: 」彪畏忠，唯唯而已。

translations.literal: " Biao feared Zhong and could only assent.
translations.idiomatic: " Biao, afraid of Zhong, murmured agreement.

sentences.zh: 已，茂為寧杲所擒，寵等相率詣京謀自首。

translations.literal: Before long Mao was seized by Ning Gao; Chong and the others in succession went to the capital intending to surrender themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Mao was seized by Ning Gao; Chong and his band set out for the capital intending to give themselves up.

sentences.zh: 忠與永成為請於帝，且曰：「必獻萬金乃赦。

translations.literal: Zhong and Yongcheng pleaded for them with the Emperor, saying: "They must pay ten thousand taels of gold before there can be pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong and Yongcheng interceded with the Emperor, adding, "They must pay ten thousand taels in gold before a pardon can be granted.

sentences.zh: 」寵、宸不能辦，逃去。

translations.literal: " Chong and Chen could not meet the sum and fled.
translations.idiomatic: " Unable to raise the sum, Chong and Chen fled.

sentences.zh: 既而瑾誅，有詔許自首。

translations.literal: Later, when Jin was executed, an edict permitted voluntary surrender.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin's fall, an edict allowed those who surrendered themselves.

sentences.zh: 寵等乃出詣官。

translations.literal: Chong and the others then came forth and reported to the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: Chong and his followers then emerged and submitted to the officials.

sentences.zh: 兵部奏赦之，令捕他盜自效。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War memorialized to pardon them and ordered them to capture other bandits to redeem themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War recommended their pardon and ordered them to capture other bandits as proof of merit.

sentences.zh: 寵等憚要束，未幾復叛。

translations.literal: Chong and the others feared the constraints and before long rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: Fearful of the restrictions placed on them, they soon rose again.

sentences.zh: 黨日眾，所至，陷城殺將吏。

translations.literal: Their party grew daily; wherever they went they stormed cities and killed commanders and officials.
translations.idiomatic: Their following swelled daily; wherever they marched they took cities and slew commanders and officials.

sentences.zh: 中錫等受命出師，敗賊於彰德，既又敗之河間，進左都御史。

translations.literal: Zhongxi and the others took command and marched out; they defeated the bandits at Zhangde, then defeated them again at Hejian; he was advanced to Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxi took the field, routed the bandits at Zhangde, routed them again at Hejian, and was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 然賊方熾，諸將率畏懦，莫敢當其鋒，或反與之結。

translations.literal: Yet the bandits were then at their height; the generals for the most part were timid and would not meet their edge, and some even colluded with them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the rebels were at flood tide; most generals quailed before their assaults, and some even made common cause with them.

sentences.zh: 參將桑玉嘗遇賊文安村中。

translations.literal: Assistant regional commander Sang Yu once encountered the bandits in a village of Wen'an.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant regional commander Sang Yu once ran into the bandits in a Wen'an village.

sentences.zh: 寵、宸窘蹙，跳民家樓上，欲自剄。

translations.literal: Chong and Chen were hard pressed; they leaped onto a commoner's upper story and were about to slash their throats.
translations.idiomatic: Chong and Chen, trapped, scrambled onto a villager's upper story and were on the verge of suicide.

sentences.zh: 而玉素受賊賂，故緩之。

translations.literal: But Yu had long taken bribes from the bandits and therefore held back.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, long on the bandits' payroll, deliberately held back.

sentences.zh: 有頃，彥名持大刀至，殺傷數十人，大呼抵樓下。

translations.literal: Before long Yanming arrived bearing a great blade, wounding several dozen men and shouting up to the tower.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Qi Yanming arrived with a great blade, cut down dozens, and roared at the foot of the tower.

sentences.zh: 寵、宸知救至，出，射殺數人。

translations.literal: Chong and Chen knew rescue had come; they came out and shot several men dead.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing rescue at hand, Chong and Chen descended and shot several soldiers dead.

sentences.zh: 玉大敗。

translations.literal: Yu suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was routed.

sentences.zh: 參將宋振禦賊棗強，不發一矢，城遂陷，死者七千人。

translations.literal: Assistant regional commander Song Zhen faced the bandits at Zaoqiang and did not loose a single arrow; the city fell and seven thousand perished.
translations.idiomatic: At Zaoqiang, assistant regional commander Song Zhen faced the bandits yet never drew a bow; the city fell and seven thousand died.

sentences.zh: 當是時，寵、宸等自畿輔犯山東、河南，南下湖廣，抵江西。

translations.literal: At this time Chong, Chen, and the others from the capital region invaded Shandong and Henan, swept south into Huguang, and pressed into Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Chong, Chen, and their host ranged from the capital region through Shandong and Henan, south into Huguang, and on into Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 復自南而北，直窺霸州。

translations.literal: They turned from the south back north and drove straight toward Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wheeling north again, they drove straight toward Bazhou.

sentences.zh: 楊虎等由河北入山西，復東抵文安，與寵等合，破邑百數，縱橫數千里，所過若無人。

translations.literal: Yang Hu and others entered Shanxi from Hebei, then turned east to Wen'an and joined Chong; they stormed over a hundred settlements and ranged thousands of li as if no one stood in their way.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu's band crossed from Hebei into Shanxi, swept east to Wen'an to unite with Chong, and overran a hundred towns across thousands of li as though the land were empty.

sentences.zh: 中錫雖有時望，不習兵。

translations.literal: Although Zhongxi enjoyed some repute, he was not versed in military matters.
translations.idiomatic: Respected though he was, Zhongxi knew nothing of war.

sentences.zh: 偉亦紈袴子，見賊強，諸將怯，度不能破賊，乃議招撫。

translations.literal: Wei too was a silk-stocking scion; seeing the bandits strong and the generals cowed, he judged that they could not be broken and so proposed appeasement.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was a pampered nobleman's son; seeing the rebels' strength and the generals' fear, he concluded they could not be crushed and urged pacification.

sentences.zh: 謂盜本良民，由酷吏寧杲與中官貪黷所激，若推誠待之，可毋戰降也。

translations.literal: He said the robbers were originally good people, provoked by the harsh official Ning Gao and by greedy eunuchs; if treated with sincerity they could be won without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: The brigands, he argued, had been ordinary folk driven to arms by Ning Gao's cruelty and eunuch corruption—treat them honestly and they would submit without a battle.

sentences.zh: 遂下令：賊所在勿捕，過勿邀擊，饑渴則食飲之，降者待以不死。

translations.literal: He then issued orders: where bandits were, do not seize them; pass them by without ambush; if they hunger or thirst give them food and drink; those who surrender are to be spared death.
translations.idiomatic: Orders went out: do not arrest bandits in their path, do not intercept them in transit, feed the hungry, and spare those who yielded.

sentences.zh: 賊聞，欲就撫，相戒毋焚掠。

translations.literal: Hearing this, the bandits wished to accept pacification and cautioned one another against burning and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels, hearing this, inclined toward surrender and warned one another against looting.

sentences.zh: 猶豫未定。

translations.literal: They still hesitated, unable to decide.
translations.idiomatic: They wavered, unable to commit.

sentences.zh: 而朝廷以京軍弱，議發邊兵。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the court, finding the capital army weak, debated mobilizing frontier troops.
translations.idiomatic: The court, judging the capital force too weak, debated sending frontier troops.

sentences.zh: 中錫欲戰，則兵未集，欲撫，則賊時向背，終不得要領。

translations.literal: Zhongxi wished to fight but the troops were not yet assembled; he wished to pacify but the bandits wavered back and forth, and in the end he could gain no clear leverage.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxi wanted to fight, yet the armies were not ready; he wanted to negotiate, yet the bandits kept shifting—he never gained a firm grip.

sentences.zh: 既建議主撫，不能變。

translations.literal: Having already advocated appeasement, he could not change course.
translations.idiomatic: Having committed to appeasement, he could not turn back.

sentences.zh: 會寵等聞邊兵且至，退屯德州桑園。

translations.literal: When Chong and the others heard that frontier troops were about to arrive, they withdrew and encamped at Sangyuan in Dezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that frontier troops were coming, Chong's band fell back to camp at Sangyuan in Dezhou.

sentences.zh: 中錫肩輿入其營，與酒食，開誠慰諭之。

translations.literal: Zhongxi entered their camp in a sedan chair, gave them wine and food, and spoke to them frankly with comfort and admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxi rode a sedan into their camp, feasted them, and addressed them with open-hearted counsel.

sentences.zh: 眾拜且泣，送馬為壽。

translations.literal: The multitude bowed and wept, presenting a horse as a gift of longevity.
translations.idiomatic: The host bowed and wept, presenting a horse as a token of respect.

sentences.zh: 寵慷慨請降，宸乃仰天咨嗟曰：「騎虎不得下。

translations.literal: Chong magnanimously offered to surrender; Chen then looked skyward and sighed: "Riding a tiger, one cannot dismount.
translations.idiomatic: Chong generously offered submission; Chen gazed heavenward and sighed, "Riding a tiger—there is no getting off.

sentences.zh: 今奄臣柄國，人所知也。

translations.literal: Today eunuchs hold the state; everyone knows it.
translations.idiomatic: Today the eunuchs hold the realm—every man knows it.

sentences.zh: 馬都堂能自主乎？

translations.literal: Can Lord Ma truly act on his own authority?
translations.idiomatic: Can Lord Ma truly decide for himself?

sentences.zh: 」遂罷會。

translations.literal: " The meeting was then dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: " With that the parley broke up.

sentences.zh: 而是時方詔懸賞格購賊。

translations.literal: At this very time an edict had just proclaimed a bounty list for purchasing bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Just then, too, the throne had posted bounties for the rebels' heads.

sentences.zh: 寵等偵知之，益疑懼，徑去，焚掠如故。

translations.literal: Chong and the others learned of it, grew all the more suspicious and afraid, went straight away, and plundered as before.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of the bounties, they grew doubly fearful, marched off at once, and resumed their ravaging.

sentences.zh: 獨至故城，戒毋犯馬都堂家。

translations.literal: Only when they reached Gucheng did they warn that Lord Ma's household was not to be touched.
translations.idiomatic: Only at Gucheng did they order that Lord Ma's house be left alone.

sentences.zh: 由是，中錫謗大起，謂其以家故縱賊。

translations.literal: Because of this slander against Zhongxi swelled, saying that for his family's sake he had allowed the bandits to go.
translations.idiomatic: Slander swelled against Zhongxi—that he had let the bandits run free to protect his own home.

sentences.zh: 言官交劾之，下詔切責。

translations.literal: Censors in succession impeached him; the throne issued a stern reprimand.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate piled on accusations; an edict rebuked him sharply.

sentences.zh: 中錫猶堅持其說以請。

translations.literal: Zhongxi still held to his view in his requests.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxi still pressed his case for appeasement.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書何鑒謂「賊誠解甲則貰死，即不然，毋為所誑」。

translations.literal: Minister of War He Jian said: "If the bandits truly lay down arms, spare their lives; if not, do not be deceived by them."
translations.idiomatic: Minister He Jian cautioned: "If they truly disarm, spare them; otherwise, do not be gulled."

sentences.zh: 既而寵等終不降，乃遣侍郎陸完督師，而召中錫、偉還。

translations.literal: Before long Chong and the others still would not submit; Vice Minister Lu Wan was dispatched to supervise the army, and Zhongxi and Wei were recalled.
translations.idiomatic: When Chong still would not yield, Vice Minister Lu Wan was sent to take command and Zhongxi and Wei were recalled.

sentences.zh: 初，中錫受命討賊，大學士楊廷和謂楊一清曰：「彼文士耳，不足任也。

translations.literal: When Zhongxi first received orders to suppress the bandits, Grand Secretary Yang Tinghe had told Yang Yiqing: "He is a literary man—not fit for the task.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongxi first took orders against the bandits, Grand Secretary Yang Tinghe told Yang Yiqing, "He is a literatus—hardly equal to the task.

sentences.zh: 」竟無功，與偉同下獄論死。

translations.literal: " In the end he achieved no merit; together with Wei he was cast into prison and sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: " He achieved nothing; he and Wei were imprisoned and condemned to death.

sentences.zh: 中錫死獄中，偉革爵。

translations.literal: Zhongxi died in prison; Wei was stripped of his rank.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxi died in his cell; Wei lost his title.

sentences.zh: 十一年，巡按御史盧雍追訟中錫冤，謂：「賊實聽撫，僉事許承芳忌之，潛請益兵，疑賊心。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year touring censor Lu Yong pursued the charge of Zhongxi's injustice, saying: "The bandits truly heeded the pacification; Junior Vice Commissioner Xu Chengfang, envious, secretly requested more troops and sowed doubt in the bandits' hearts.
translations.idiomatic: In year eleven, touring censor Lu Yong memorialized Zhongxi's wrong, arguing that the bandits had been ready to submit until Junior Vice Commissioner Xu Chengfang, jealous, secretly sought reinforcements and unsettled them.

sentences.zh: 及賊再受約，方至軍門，而檻車已就道矣。

translations.literal: When the bandits came to accept the terms a second time and had just reached army headquarters, the prisoner cart was already on the road.
translations.idiomatic: When they came a second time to accept terms and reached headquarters, the prisoner cart was already rolling.

sentences.zh: 」朝廷乃復中錫官，賜祭，予蔭。

translations.literal: " The court thereupon restored Zhongxi's office, bestowed sacrificial rites, and granted hereditary privilege.
translations.idiomatic: The throne restored his rank, granted sacrificial honors, and awarded hereditary privilege to his heirs.

sentences.zh: 陸完，字全卿，長洲人。

translations.literal: Lu Wan, style name Quanqing, was a man of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Wan, whose style name was Quanqing, was a native of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 為諸生。

translations.literal: He was a student in the prefectural school.
translations.idiomatic: He studied as a prefectural-school student.

sentences.zh: 中官王敬至蘇，以事庭曳諸生。

translations.literal: When the eunuch Wang Jing came to Suzhou, on a legal matter he dragged students into court.
translations.idiomatic: When the eunuch Wang Jing came to Suzhou, he dragged students into court over a legal dispute.

sentences.zh: 諸生競起擊之，完不與。

translations.literal: The students surged up to strike him; Wan did not join them.
translations.idiomatic: The students rushed to beat him; Wan held back.

sentences.zh: 惡完者中之，敬遂首列完名上聞。

translations.literal: Those who hated Wan slandered him; Jing therefore listed Wan's name first in his report to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Wan's enemies libeled him, and Jing put Wan's name first in his memorial to the throne.

sentences.zh: 巡撫王恕極論敬罪，完乃得免。

translations.literal: Grand coordinator Wang Su argued forcefully for Jing's crime; Wan then escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Wang Su argued Jing's guilt with force; Wan was spared.

sentences.zh: 舉成化二十三年進士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Chenghua he passed the metropolitan examination as a graduate.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in Chenghua 23.

sentences.zh: 謁選，恕方為吏部，曰：「是嘗擊奄人者，當為御史。

translations.literal: At his assignment audience, Su—then at the Ministry of Personnel—said: "This is the man who once struck the palace eunuchs; he ought to be made a censor.
translations.idiomatic: When he came forward for appointment, Wang Su, who was then at the Board of Personnel, said: "Here is the student who once struck the palace eunuchs—he should be made a censor.

sentences.zh: 」入臺，果有聲。

translations.literal: " On entering the Censorate, he indeed gained a reputation.
translations.idiomatic: " Once he entered the Censorate, his name quickly carried weight.

sentences.zh: 正德初，歷江西按察使。

translations.literal: Early in the Zhengde reign, he served in succession as Jiangxi surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Zhengde reign he rose through service as Jiangxi surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 寧王宸濠雅重之，時召預曲宴，以金罍為贈。

translations.literal: The Prince of Ning, Zhu Chenhao, greatly esteemed him, often summoning him to private banquets and presenting him with a gold libation cup.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Ning Zhu Chenhao held him in high regard, frequently called him to intimate feasts, and gave him a gold libation vessel.

sentences.zh: 三年冬，擢右僉都御史，巡撫宣府。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-chief and made grand coordinator of Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, winter, he was elevated to Right Vice Censor-in-chief and appointed grand coordinator of Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾惡完赴闕後期，命以試職視事。

translations.literal: Liu Jin hated Wan for arriving late at court after his appointment and ordered him to assume duties on probationary appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin resented Wan for being late to the capital after his appointment and made him serve on a probationary commission.

sentences.zh: 明年夏，復改南院，督江防軍。

translations.literal: The following summer he was again transferred to the Southern Yamen to supervise Yangtze defense forces.
translations.idiomatic: Next summer he was reassigned to the Southern Yamen to command river-defense troops.

sentences.zh: 完以都御史試職非故事，懼甚，賄瑾，召為左僉都御史。

translations.literal: Wan feared greatly that serving as censor-in-chief on probation was without precedent; he bribed Jin and was summoned back as Left Vice Censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Wan was deeply afraid, for a probationary censor-in-chiefship was unprecedented; he bribed Jin and was recalled as Left Vice Censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 五年春，拜兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifth year he was appointed Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, spring, he received appointment as Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 瑾敗，言者劾其黨附，帝不問。

translations.literal: When Jin fell, memorialists impeached Wan for party affiliation; the emperor did not pursue it.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin's downfall, critics impeached Wan as one of his faction, but the emperor took no action.

sentences.zh: 明年，霸州賊劉六、劉七等起，奉楊虎為首。

translations.literal: The following year bandits Liu Six and Liu Seven rose in Bazhou, with Yang Hu as their leader.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Liu Six and Liu Seven rebelled in Bazhou and made Yang Hu their chief.

sentences.zh: 惠安伯張偉、右都御史馬中錫師出無功，逮系論死。

translations.literal: Pacification Earl Zhang Wei and Right Censor-in-chief Ma Zhongxi led troops out without success and were arrested and sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification Earl Zhang Wei and Right Censor-in-chief Ma Zhongxi marched out without result, were seized, and condemned to death.

sentences.zh: 八月，詔完兼右僉都御史提督軍務，統京營、宣府、延綏軍討之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month an edict ordered Wan also to hold Right Vice Censor-in-chief and take charge of military affairs, commanding Capital Garrisons, Xuanfu, and Yansui troops to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Wan was ordered to add the title Right Vice Censor-in-chief and direct military affairs, uniting Capital Garrisons, Xuanfu, and Yansui forces against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 行及涿州，忽傳賊且逼京師，命還軍入衛。

translations.literal: When the army reached Zhuozhou, suddenly word came that the bandits were about to threaten the capital; he was ordered to return the army to guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Marching as far as Zhuozhou, he was suddenly told the bandits were nearing the capital and ordered to turn the army back to defend it.

sentences.zh: 會副總兵許泰、遊擊郤永等敗楊虎等於霸州，賊南走，京師始解嚴。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Vice Commander-in-chief Xu Tai and Mobile Corps Commander Xi Yong defeated Yang Hu and others at Bazhou; the bandits fled south, and the capital at last lifted its alert.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Vice Commander Xu Tai and Mobile Corps Commander Xi Yong routed Yang Hu at Bazhou; the rebels fled south and the capital finally stood down from alert.

sentences.zh: 指揮賀勇等再敗賊信安，副總兵馮楨復大敗之阜城，分兵追擊。

translations.literal: Commander He Yong and others defeated the bandits again at Xin'an; Vice Commander-in-chief Feng Zhen inflicted a major defeat on them at Fucheng, and troops were sent in separate columns to pursue.
translations.idiomatic: Commander He Yong beat them again at Xin'an; Vice Commander Feng Zhen crushed them at Fucheng, and detachments were sent in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 賊東圍滄州。

translations.literal: The bandits turned east to besiege Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels swung east and laid siege to Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 會劉六、七中流矢，乃解而南，陷山東縣二十。

translations.literal: When Liu Six and Seven were struck by arrows, they then lifted the siege and went south, seizing twenty counties in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Six and Seven took arrow wounds, broke off the siege, and drove south, overrunning twenty Shandong counties.

sentences.zh: 楊虎兵亦北殘威縣、新河。

translations.literal: Yang Hu's forces also ravaged northward through Wei County and Xinhe.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu's band ravaged Wei County and Xinhe as it pushed north.

sentences.zh: 於是完頻請濟師。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wan repeatedly petitioned for reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: Wan then pleaded again and again for more troops.

sentences.zh: 益發遼東、山西諸鎮兵逐賊。

translations.literal: Troops were further dispatched from the Liaodong, Shanxi, and other garrisons to hunt the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Additional forces were sent from Liaodong, Shanxi, and other garrisons to run the bandits down.

sentences.zh: 賊益南，圍濟寧，焚運舟，轉寇曹州。

translations.literal: The bandits pressed further south, besieged Jining, burned grain-transport boats, and turned to plunder Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels drove farther south, besieged Jining, torched grain barges, and swung to raid Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 楨、泰、永擊斬二千余人，獲其魁朱諒。

translations.literal: Feng Zhen, Xu Tai, and Yong killed and beheaded more than two thousand, capturing their chieftain Zhu Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Zhen, Xu Tai, and Xi Yong killed over two thousand and seized their leader Zhu Liang.

sentences.zh: 錄功，進完右都御史，諸將皆增秩。

translations.literal: Merits were recorded; Wan was promoted to Right Censor-in-chief, and all the generals received rank increases.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards were entered in the record: Wan was made Right Censor-in-chief and every commander gained rank.

sentences.zh: 中官谷大用、張忠意賊旦暮平，乃自請督師。

translations.literal: The eunuchs Gu Dayong and Zhang Zhong thought the bandits would be pacified any day and volunteered to supervise the army themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs Gu Dayong and Zhang Zhong, believing the rebels would fall within days, asked to take command in person.

sentences.zh: 詔以大用總督軍務，伏羌伯毛銳充總兵官，忠監神槍，統京軍五千人，會完討賊。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Dayong grand coordinator of military affairs, Mao Rui of Fuyang made commander-in-chief, Zhong to supervise the divine guns, with five thousand Capital troops—they would join Wan to attack the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Dayong grand coordinator of military affairs, the Earl of Fuyang Mao Rui commander-in-chief, and Zhong overseer of the divine guns, with five thousand capital troops to join Wan against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 時劉六等縱橫沂、莒間，而楊虎陷宿遷，執淮安知府劉祥、靈璧知縣陳伯安，連陷虹、永城、虞城、夏邑及歸德州。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Six and others ranged between Yi and Ju, while Yang Hu seized Suqian, took Huai'an prefect Liu Xiang and Lingbi magistrate Chen Bo'an captive, and in succession seized Hong, Yongcheng, Yucheng, Xiayi, and Guizhou prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Six roamed between Yi and Ju while Yang Hu took Suqian, seized Huai'an prefect Liu Xiang and Lingbi magistrate Chen Bo'an, and overran Hong, Yongcheng, Yucheng, Xiayi, and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 邊兵追及，賊退至小黃河渡口。

translations.literal: Frontier troops caught up; the bandits fell back to the Little Yellow River ford.
translations.idiomatic: Border troops overtook them and the rebels retreated to the Little Yellow River crossing.

sentences.zh: 百戶夏時設伏蹙之，虎溺死。

translations.literal: Company Commander Xia Shi set an ambush and pressed them; Hu drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Company Commander Xia Shi ambushed and harried them; Yang Hu drowned.

sentences.zh: 余賊奔河南，推劉惠為首，大敗副總兵白玉軍，攻陷沈丘，殺都指揮王保，執都指揮潘翀，北陷鹿邑。

translations.literal: The remaining bandits fled to Henan, made Liu Hui their leader, routed Vice Commander-in-chief Bai Yu's army, stormed Shenqiu, killed Regional Commander Wang Bao, took Regional Commander Pan Chong captive, and pushed north to seize Luyi.
translations.idiomatic: The survivors fled into Henan, set up Liu Hui as chief, shattered Vice Commander Bai Yu, stormed Shenqiu, killed Regional Commander Wang Bao, seized Regional Commander Pan Chong, and pushed north into Luyi.

sentences.zh: 有陳翰者，與寧龍謀奉惠為奉天征討大元帥，趙鐩副之。

translations.literal: One Chen Han, with Ning Long, plotted to install Hui as Commander-in-chief for Punitive Campaigns in Compliance with Heaven; Zhao Sui was to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Chen Han joined Ning Long in proposing Liu Hui as "Commander-in-chief for Heaven's Punitive Campaign," with Zhao Sui as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 翰自為侍謀軍國重務元帥府長史，與龍立東西二廠治事。

translations.literal: Han styled himself Chief Secretary of the Marshal's Bureau for Planning Army and State Affairs; with Long he set up Eastern and Western factories to conduct affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Han took the title Chief Secretary of the Marshal's Bureau for Army and State Planning; he and Long established Eastern and Western "factories" to run their government.

sentences.zh: 分其軍為二十八營，以應列宿，營各置都督，聚眾至十三萬。

translations.literal: They divided their army into twenty-eight camps corresponding to the lunar mansions; each camp had its own commander-in-chief, and their forces gathered to one hundred thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: They split the host into twenty-eight camps mapped to the lunar mansions, each with its own commander, until their numbers reached one hundred thirty thousand.

sentences.zh: 欲牽制官軍，於是惠、鐩擾河南，劉六及齊彥名等擾山東，黨分為二。

translations.literal: To tie down government troops, Hui and Sui harried Henan while Liu Six and Qi Yanming and others harried Shandong—the party split in two.
translations.idiomatic: To pin down imperial armies, Hui and Sui ravaged Henan while Liu Six, Qi Yanming, and others ravaged Shandong—the rebel force divided in two.

sentences.zh: 已而六復轉而北，永敗之濰縣。

translations.literal: Before long Six turned north again; Yong defeated him at Wei County.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Liu Six swung north again; Xi Yong defeated him at Wei County.

sentences.zh: 還趨霸州，帝將出郊省牲，聞之懼，急召完赴援，完擊破之文安。

translations.literal: He then dashed toward Bazhou; the emperor was about to go to the suburbs to inspect the sacrificial animals, and on hearing this was alarmed, urgently summoned Wan to reinforce; Wan routed them at Wen'an.
translations.idiomatic: They raced toward Bazhou just as the emperor was to inspect the sacrificial oxen in the suburbs; alarmed, he urgently recalled Wan, who smashed them at Wen'an.

sentences.zh: 賊南至湯陰，完又督諸將追敗之，先後俘斬千人。

translations.literal: The bandits went south as far as Tangyin; Wan again directed the generals in pursuit and defeated them, capturing and slaying a thousand in all.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels pushed south to Tangyin; Wan again drove the commanders in pursuit and took a thousand heads between capture and kill.

sentences.zh: 當是時，六等眾號數萬，然多脅從，精銳不過千余人。

translations.literal: At this time the forces of Six and the others were said to number tens of thousands, yet most were coerced followers; crack troops did not exceed a thousand-odd.
translations.idiomatic: By then Liu Six's host was said to number in the tens of thousands, but most were pressed into service; hardened fighters were barely a thousand.

sentences.zh: 自兵部下首功令，官軍追賊，賊輒驅良民前行，急則棄所掠逸去。

translations.literal: Since the ordinance on reporting heads as merit, whenever government troops pursued bandits the bandits would drive good civilians ahead; pressed hard, they would abandon their loot and flee.
translations.idiomatic: Once the military rewarded severed heads, pursuers found rebels driving civilians before them; hard pressed, the bandits dropped their plunder and slipped away.

sentences.zh: 官軍所殺皆良民，以故捷書屢奏，而賊勢不衰。

translations.literal: Those the government troops killed were all good civilians; thus victory reports were repeatedly filed while the bandit strength did not wane.
translations.idiomatic: Government kills were mostly innocents, so victory memorials piled up even as rebel power never faded.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，六等復突霸州，京師戒嚴。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year, Six and others again burst into Bazhou, and the capital went on alert.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the next year Liu Six broke into Bazhou again and the capital re-entered emergency.

sentences.zh: 詔完及大用、銳還禦近畿，賊乃西掠博野，攻蠡縣、臨城。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Wan and Dayong and Rui back to defend the near capital region; the bandits then raided west through Boye and attacked Li and Lincheng counties.
translations.idiomatic: Wan, Dayong, and Rui were ordered back to shield the capital approaches; the rebels swept west through Boye and struck Li and Lincheng.

sentences.zh: 大用、銳與遇於長垣，大敗。

translations.literal: Dayong and Rui encountered them at Changyuan and suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Dayong and Rui met them at Changyuan and were routed.

sentences.zh: 廷議召二人還，別命都御史彭澤同鹹寧伯仇鉞辦河南賊，以畿輔、山東賊委完。

translations.literal: Court deliberation recalled the two, separately ordering Censor-in-chief Peng Ze together with Pacification Earl Qiu Yao to handle the Henan bandits, while entrusting Capital Region and Shandong bandits to Wan.
translations.idiomatic: The court recalled the two eunuch commanders and gave Censor-in-chief Peng Ze and Pacification Earl Qiu Yao the Henan rebels, leaving the capital districts and Shandong to Wan.

sentences.zh: 完遣永追敗劉六於宋家莊。

translations.literal: Wan sent Yong to pursue and defeat Liu Six at Song Family Village.
translations.idiomatic: Wan dispatched Xi Yong, who ran Liu Six down and beat him at Song Family Village.

sentences.zh: 賊南犯滕縣，副總兵劉暉大敗之，賊遂奔登、萊海套。

translations.literal: The bandits invaded south to Teng County; Vice Commander-in-chief Liu Hui defeated them badly; the bandits then fled to the Deng-Lai coastal enclaves.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels struck south into Teng County; Vice Commander Liu Hui crushed them, and they fled toward the Deng-Lai coast.

sentences.zh: 完師次平度，檄永、玉與遊擊溫恭三道進攻，命副總兵張俊、李鋐及泰、暉分軍邀其奔逸。

translations.literal: Wan's army halted at Pingdu; he ordered Yong, Yu, and Mobile Corps Commander Wen Gong in three columns to attack, and commanded Vice Commanders Zhang Jun, Li Gang, and Tai and Hui to divide forces and intercept their escape.
translations.idiomatic: Wan halted at Pingdu, sent Yong, Bai Yu, and Mobile Corps Commander Wen Gong in three thrusts, and set Vice Commanders Zhang Jun, Li Gang, Xu Tai, and Liu Hui to block escape routes.

sentences.zh: 賊走，連戰皆大敗之，賊乃變服易馬而遁，先後擒斬二千六百余人。

translations.literal: The bandits fled; in successive engagements they were badly defeated; the bandits then changed clothes and horses to escape; in all more than two thousand six hundred were captured and slain.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels ran; battle after battle went against them until they swapped clothes and mounts to flee; captures and kills together exceeded twenty-six hundred.

sentences.zh: 賊止三百人北走，沿途招聚，勢復張。

translations.literal: Only three hundred bandits fled north, gathering recruits along the way until their strength swelled again.
translations.idiomatic: Barely three hundred rebels fled north, recruiting as they went until their force swelled anew.

sentences.zh: 剽香河、寶坻、玉田，轉攻武清。

translations.literal: They plundered Xianghe, Baodi, and Yutian, then turned to attack Wuqing.
translations.idiomatic: They raided Xianghe, Baodi, and Yutian, then wheeled on Wuqing.

sentences.zh: 遊擊王杲敗沒，巡撫寧杲兵亦敗，畿輔復震動。

translations.literal: Mobile Corps Commander Wang Gao was defeated and lost; Grand Coordinator Ning Gao's troops were also beaten—the Capital Region was shaken anew.
translations.idiomatic: Mobile Corps Commander Wang Gao was wiped out; Grand Coordinator Ning Gao's men were beaten too, and the capital approaches trembled again.

sentences.zh: 而賊轉南至冠縣，暉襲敗之，指揮張勛又敗之平原。

translations.literal: The bandits then turned south to Guan County; Hui caught and defeated them; Commander Zhang Xun defeated them again at Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels turned south to Guan County; Liu Hui struck and broke them; Commander Zhang Xun beat them again at Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 賊南奔邳州，渡河抵固始。

translations.literal: The bandits fled south to Pizhou, crossed the river, and reached Gushi.
translations.idiomatic: They fled south to Pizhou, crossed the river, and entered Gushi.

sentences.zh: 會河南賊已平，劉六等勢益衰，遂走湖廣。

translations.literal: By then the Henan bandits had been pacified; Liu Six and the others grew weaker still, and fled to Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Henan was already quiet; Liu Six's remnant weakened further and bolted for Huguang.

sentences.zh: 奪舟到夏口，遇都御史馬炳然，殺之。

translations.literal: Seizing boats they reached Xiakou, encountered Censor-in-chief Ma Bingran, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: They seized boats to Xiakou, met Censor-in-chief Ma Bingran, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 復登陸，焚漢口，為指揮滿弼等追及，劉六中流矢，與子仲淮赴水死。

translations.literal: They went ashore again, burned Hankou; pursued by Commander Man Bi and others, Liu Six was struck by an arrow and drowned in the river with his son Zhonghuai.
translations.idiomatic: Back on land they burned Hankou; Commander Man Bi and others overtook them; Liu Six took an arrow and drowned with his son Zhonghuai.

sentences.zh: 劉七、齊彥名率五百人舟行，自黃州順流抵鎮江。

translations.literal: Liu Seven and Qi Yanming led five hundred men by boat, from Huangzhou downstream to Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Seven and Qi Yanming took five hundred men by boat from Huangzhou down the current to Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 南京告急，完疾趨而南。

translations.literal: Nanjing reported emergency; Wan hastened south.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing sounded the alarm; Wan raced south.

sentences.zh: 帝命彭澤、仇鉞會完軍進剿。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Peng Ze and Qiu Yao to join Wan's army in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered Peng Ze and Qiu Yao to unite with Wan's force for the pursuit.

sentences.zh: 大兵盡集江南、北，賊猶乘潮上下肆掠。

translations.literal: When the main forces had all gathered in Jiangnan and north of the river, the bandits still rode the tides up and down, plundering at will.
translations.idiomatic: Though armies massed on both banks, the rebels still rode the tides up and down, looting at will.

sentences.zh: 操江武靖伯趙弘澤、都御史陳世良遇之，敗績，死者無算。

translations.literal: River-defense Pacification Earl Zhao Hongze and Censor-in-chief Chen Shiliang encountered them, suffered defeat, and the dead were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: River-defense Pacification Earl Zhao Hongze and Censor-in-chief Chen Shiliang met them, were shattered, and the dead could not be counted.

sentences.zh: 七月，賊治舟孟瀆。

translations.literal: In the seventh month the bandits fitted out boats at Mengdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the rebels outfitted boats at Mengdu.

sentences.zh: 完等至鎮江，留鉞防守，令恭以騎駐江北，暉、永以舟趨江陰，完率都指揮孫文、傅鎧趨福山港。

translations.literal: When Wan and the others reached Zhenjiang, he left Qiu Yao to defend, ordered Gong with cavalry to hold the north bank, Hui and Yong with boats to hurry to Jiangyin, and Wan himself led Regional Commanders Sun Wen and Fu Kai toward Fushan Harbor.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhenjiang Wan left Qiu Yao on defense, posted Wen Gong's cavalry on the north bank, sent Liu Hui and Xi Yong by water toward Jiangyin, and himself led Regional Commanders Sun Wen and Fu Kai to Fushan Harbor.

sentences.zh: 賊懼，抵通州。

translations.literal: The bandits were afraid and made for Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, the rebels made for Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 颶風大作，棄舟走保狼山。

translations.literal: A hurricane rose; they abandoned their boats and fled to hold Lang Mountain.
