translations.idiomatic: A typhoon rose; they abandoned their fleet and fled to Lang Mountain.

sentences.zh: 完命同知羅瑋夜導軍登山南蹙之。

translations.literal: Wan ordered Vice Prefect Luo Wei to guide the army by night up the mountain's south slope and press them.
translations.idiomatic: Wan had Vice Prefect Luo Wei lead troops by night up the southern slope to hem them in.

sentences.zh: 彥名中槍死，七中矢亦赴水死，余賊盡平。

translations.literal: Yanming was shot and died; Seven was also struck by arrows and drowned; the remaining bandits were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Yanming fell to gunfire; Liu Seven took arrows and drowned too; the rest were wiped out.

sentences.zh: 還朝，進完太子少保左都御史，蔭子錦衣世百戶。

translations.literal: On return to court, Wan was promoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Left Censor-in-chief; his son was granted hereditary rank as a hundred-household guardsman in the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Back at court he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Left Censor-in-chief; his son received hereditary rank as an Embroidered Uniform Guard centurion.

sentences.zh: 明年代何鑒為兵部尚書。

translations.literal: The next year he replaced He Jian as Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he succeeded He Jian as Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 完有才智，急功名，善交權勢。

translations.literal: Wan had talent and wisdom, was eager for fame, and adept at cultivating the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: Wan was clever and ambitious, hungry for reputation and skilled at courting power.

sentences.zh: 劉暉、許泰、江彬皆其部將，後並寵幸用事，完遂行其力。

translations.literal: Liu Hui, Xu Tai, and Jiang Bin were all his subordinate generals; later all won favor and wielded power—Wan thereby exerted their strength.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hui, Xu Tai, and Jiang Bin had all served under him; each later won the emperor's favor and office—Wan drew on their strength.

sentences.zh: 時宸濠已萌異志。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Ning had already begun to harbor separatist designs.
translations.idiomatic: By then Prince of Ning Zhu Chenhao already nursed rebellion in his heart.

sentences.zh: 聞完為兵部，致書盛陳舊好，欲復護衛及屯田。

translations.literal: Hearing Wan was at the Ministry of War, he sent a letter lavishly rehearsing old friendship, wishing to restore his bodyguard and military colonies.
translations.idiomatic: Learning Wan headed the Ministry of War, the prince wrote at length of old friendship, seeking restoration of his bodyguard and military colonies.

sentences.zh: 完答書，令以祖制為詞。

translations.literal: Wan replied with a letter that used ancestral institutions as its pretext.
translations.idiomatic: Wan answered in a letter that cited ancestral precedent as refusal.

sentences.zh: 宸濠遂遣人輦金帛巨萬，寓所善教坊臧賢家，遍遺用事貴人，屬錢寧為內主。

translations.literal: The Prince then sent men with tens of thousands in gold and silk to the home of his favorite, the music-office performer Zang Xian, distributing gifts widely among powerful men at court, with Qian Ning as his inside advocate.
translations.idiomatic: The prince then carted gold and silks worth tens of thousands to the house of his favorite, music-office performer Zang Xian, showering gifts on court power-brokers through Qian Ning as inside broker.

sentences.zh: 比奏下，完遂為復請，而以屯田屬戶部，請付廷議。

translations.literal: When the memorial reached the throne, Wan then submitted a request for restoration on the Prince's behalf, while referring military colonies to the Ministry of Revenue and asking that it be put to court debate.
translations.idiomatic: When the petition arrived, Wan himself memorialized to restore the bodyguard while handing the colonies to the Ministry of Revenue for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 內閣擬旨上，並予之。

translations.literal: The Grand Secretariat drafted the rescript for approval and granted both.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Secretariat drafted an edict approving both requests.

sentences.zh: 舉朝嘩然。

translations.literal: The whole court erupted in protest.
translations.idiomatic: The entire court exploded in outrage.

sentences.zh: 六科給事中高淓、十三道御史汪賜等力爭，章並下部，久不覆。

translations.literal: Six-Office supervising secretaries Gao Qing and thirteen-lane censors Wang Ci and others argued forcefully; memorials were sent together to the ministries, but for a long time there was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Six-Office supervising secretaries Gao Qing and censors of thirteen circuits led by Wang Ci protested fiercely; memorials went to the ministries together, yet no answer came for a long while.

sentences.zh: 南京給事中徐文溥繼言之，完乃請納諫官言，帝竟不許。

translations.literal: Nanjing supervising secretary Xu Wenpu memorialized in succession; Wan then asked to accept the remonstrators' words; the emperor ultimately refused.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing supervising secretary Xu Wenpu followed with another memorial; Wan then asked to heed the remonstrators, but the emperor would not yield.

sentences.zh: 十年改吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was moved to Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 宸濠反，就執。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Ning rebelled, he was captured on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Ning rose in rebellion, he was seized where he stood.

sentences.zh: 中官張永至南昌，搜其籍，得完平日交通事，上之。

translations.literal: Eunuch Zhang Yong reached Nanchang, searched his registers, found evidence of Wan's daily contacts, and submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch Zhang Yong reached Nanchang, searched the prince's archives, uncovered Wan's routine correspondence, and reported it.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒。

translations.literal: The emperor was furious.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 還至通州，執完。

translations.literal: Returning to Tongzhou, he arrested Wan.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march to Tongzhou he had Wan arrested.

sentences.zh: 收其母妻子女，封識其家。

translations.literal: His mother, wife, children, and daughters were taken; his house was sealed and inventoried.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, wife, sons, and daughters were seized; his home was sealed and inventoried.

sentences.zh: 比還京，反縛之竿，揭姓名於首，雜俘囚中，列凱旋前部以入，將置極刑。

translations.literal: When they returned to the capital, he was bound reversed on a pole with his name displayed on his head, mixed among captive prisoners in the van of the triumphal procession as they entered—he was to receive the extreme penalty.
translations.idiomatic: At the capital he was trussed on a pole, name pinned to his head, marched among captives at the head of the victory procession—marked for execution.

sentences.zh: 值武宗崩，世宗立，法司復奏完交外藩而遺金不卻，處護衛而執奏不堅，當斬。

translations.literal: Just then Emperor Wuzong died and Emperor Shizong ascended; the judiciary again reported that Wan, in dealings with an outer fief yet not refusing its gold, and in handling the bodyguard yet not insisting in memorial—should be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Wuzong died and Shizong took the throne; the judiciary again ruled that Wan, trafficking with an outer prince while taking his gold and weakly memorializing on the bodyguard, deserved decapitation.

sentences.zh: 完復乞哀，下廷臣覆讞。

translations.literal: Wan again begged for mercy; the case was sent down for re-adjudication by court officials.
translations.idiomatic: Wan pleaded again; the case went back to the assembled officials for review.

sentences.zh: 以平賊功，在八議之列，遂得減死，戍福建靖海衛。

translations.literal: Because of his merit in pacifying bandits he fell within the Eight Mitigations; his death sentence was reduced—he was banished to serve at Fujian's Jinghai Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His service against the great bandit rebellions placed him within the Eight Mitigations; the death sentence was commuted to exile at Fujian's Jinghai Guard.

sentences.zh: 母年九十余，竟死獄中。

translations.literal: His mother, over ninety years old, died in prison in the end.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, past ninety, died in custody.

sentences.zh: 初，完嘗夢至一山曰「大武」。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wan had dreamed of reaching a mountain called "Great Martial."
translations.idiomatic: Long before, Wan had dreamed of a mountain called Great Martial.

sentences.zh: 及抵戍所，有山如其名，嘆曰：「吾戍已久定，何所逃乎！

translations.literal: When he reached his place of exile, there was a mountain of that name; he sighed: "My exile was long since fixed—how could I escape?
translations.idiomatic: At his place of banishment he found just such a mountain and sighed: "My exile was settled long ago—where could I flee?

sentences.zh: 」竟卒於戍所。

translations.literal: " In the end he died at his place of exile.
translations.idiomatic: " He died there in the end.

sentences.zh: 洪鐘，字宣之，錢塘人。

translations.literal: Hong Zhong, style name Xuanzhi, was a man of Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Zhong, styled Xuanzhi, came from Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 成化十一年進士。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Chenghua he passed the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in Chenghua 11.

sentences.zh: 為刑部主事，遷郎中，奉命安輯江西、福建流民。

translations.literal: He served as a clerk in the Ministry of Punishments, was promoted to director, and was ordered to settle wandering populations in Jiangxi and Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the Ministry of Punishments as a clerk, rose to director, and was ordered to settle displaced people in Jiangxi and Fujian.

sentences.zh: 還言福建武平、上杭、清流、永定，江西安遠、龍南，廣東程鄉皆流移錯雜，習鬥爭，易亂，宜及平時令有司立鄉社學，教之《詩》《書》禮讓。

translations.literal: On return he reported that in Fujian Wuping, Shanghang, Qingliu, and Yongding, in Jiangxi Anyuan and Longnan, and in Guangdong's Chengxiang, migrants were mixed in disorder, practiced fighting, and were prone to rebellion—it would be well in peacetime to order local officials to establish community schools and teach them the Odes, Documents, ritual, and deference.
translations.idiomatic: Returning, he warned that Wuping, Shanghang, Qingliu, and Yongding in Fujian, Anyuan and Longnan in Jiangxi, and Chengxiang in Guangdong were jumbled with migrants who fought habitually and could rebel easily; in calm times magistrates should found village schools and teach the Odes, Documents, ritual, and courtesy.

sentences.zh: 弘治初，再遷四川按察使。

translations.literal: Early in the Hongzhi reign he was again promoted to Sichuan surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Hongzhi he was promoted again, to Sichuan surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 馬湖土知府安鰲恣淫虐，土人怨之刺骨，有司利其金置不問，遷延二十年。

translations.literal: The native prefect of Mapu, An Ao, indulged in lust and cruelty; the tribespeople hated him to the bone; officials profited from his gold and ignored the matter, which dragged on twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: Mapu native prefect An Ao reveled in lust and cruelty; the tribes hated him utterly; officials took his bribes and let the case rot for twenty years.

sentences.zh: 僉事曲銳請巡按御史張鸞按治，鐘贊決，捕鰲送京師，置極刑。

translations.literal: Assistant Commissioner Qu Rui asked the touring investigating censor Zhang Luan to conduct an inquiry; Zhong approved the decision, Ao was arrested and sent to the capital, and subjected to the extreme penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Commissioner Qu Rui petitioned Investigating Censor Zhang Luan to take the case; Hong Zhong endorsed the move, had An Ao seized and sent to the capital, and put him to death.

sentences.zh: 安氏自唐以來世有馬湖，至是改流官，一方始靖。

translations.literal: The An clan had held Mapu in hereditary succession since the Tang; at this time it was changed to regular officials, and the region was finally pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The An family had ruled Mapu since Tang times; now the post was converted to direct administration, and the area at last grew quiet.

sentences.zh: 歷江西、福建左、右布政使。

translations.literal: He served in succession as left and right administration commissioners of Jiangxi and Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to serve as left and right provincial administration commissioners in Jiangxi and Fujian.

sentences.zh: 十一年擢右副都御史，巡撫順天。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was promoted to Vice Censor-in-chief of the Right and made Grand Coordinator of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was raised to vice censor-in-chief of the right and appointed grand coordinator of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 整飭薊州邊備，建議增築塞垣。

translations.literal: He put in order the Jizhou frontier defenses and proposed enlarging the border ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: He reorganized the Jizhou frontier garrisons and urged that the border walls be extended.

sentences.zh: 自山海關西北至密雲古北口、黃花鎮直抵居庸，延亙千餘里，繕復城堡二百七十所，悉城緣邊諸縣，因奏減防秋兵六千人，歲省挽輸犒賚費數萬計。

translations.literal: From northwest of Shanhaiguan through Miyun Gubeikou and Huanghua Fort straight to Juyong, extending more than a thousand li, he restored two hundred seventy castles, walled all the border counties, and memorialized to reduce autumn-defense troops by six thousand, saving tens of thousands annually in transport and reward costs.
translations.idiomatic: From northwest of Shanhaiguan through Miyun's Gubeikou and Huanghua Fort to Juyong—over a thousand li in all—he repaired two hundred seventy strongpoints and walled every county along the frontier, then memorialized to cut six thousand autumn-defense troops, saving tens of thousands a year in haulage and reward expenses.

sentences.zh: 所部潮河川去京師二百里，居兩山間，廣百余丈，水漲成巨浸，水退則坦然平陸，寇得長驅直入。

translations.literal: The Chaohe River in his jurisdiction lay two hundred li from the capital, between two mountains, more than a hundred zhang wide; when the water rose it became a vast flood, and when it fell it was open level ground, so raiders could charge straight through.
translations.idiomatic: The Chaohe in his district stood two hundred li from the capital, boxed between two ranges and more than a hundred zhang across: in flood it became a great lake; in drought, open plain—and enemies could ride straight through.

sentences.zh: 鐘言：「關以東三里許，其山外高內庳，約余二丈，可鑿為兩渠，分殺水勢，而於口外斜築石堰以束水。

translations.literal: Zhong said: "About three li east of the pass the mountain is higher outside and lower inside, with roughly more than two zhang remaining; it can be cut into two channels to divide and reduce the water's force, and a slanting stone weir can be built outside the mouth to bind the water.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong argued: "Some three li east of the pass the slope rises outside and falls within, leaving a drop of about two zhang. Cut two channels there to split the current, and build a slanting stone dam at the mouth to hold the water back.

sentences.zh: 置關堰內，守以百人，使寇不得馳突，可免京師北顧憂，且得屯種河堧地。

translations.literal: Place the pass inside the weir and guard it with a hundred men, so that raiders cannot charge through; the capital's anxiety over the north can be avoided, and the river-bank land can be garrisoned and planted.
translations.idiomatic: Station the pass behind the dam with a hundred men so raiders cannot break through, ease the capital's fear for the northern approaches, and open the river flats to farming garrisons.

sentences.zh: 」兵部尚書馬文升等請從之。

translations.literal: " The Minister of War Ma Wensheng and others asked to follow it.
translations.idiomatic: " The Minister of War Ma Wensheng and others urged approval.

sentences.zh: 比興工，鑿山，山石崩，壓死者數百人。

translations.literal: When work was begun and the mountain was cut, the mountain rocks collapsed and several hundred were crushed to death.
translations.idiomatic: Once construction started, the cut face gave way; hundreds were buried alive.

sentences.zh: 御史弋福、給事中馬予聰等劾鐘。

translations.literal: Censor Yi Fu, Supervising Secretary Ma Yucong, and others impeached Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Yi Fu, supervising secretary Ma Yucong, and others impeached Hong Zhong.

sentences.zh: 巡撫張烜等請罷役，不聽。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Zhang Xuan and others asked to stop the labor; they were not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Zhang Xuan and others pleaded to halt the project, but the court refused.

sentences.zh: 未幾，工成，侍郎張達偕司禮中官往視。

translations.literal: Before long the work was completed; Vice Minister Zhang Da went with a Directorate eunuch to inspect it.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the works were finished; Vice Minister Zhang Da went to inspect them with a eunuch from the Directorate of Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 還言石洞僅泄小水，地近邊垣多沙石，不利耕種。

translations.literal: On return they reported that the stone tunnel only drained a little water, and the land near the border wall had much sand and stone, unfavorable for cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: They returned to report that the stone channels released only a trickle and that the ground near the wall was mostly sand and gravel—poor for farming.

sentences.zh: 給事中屈伸等劾鐘欺妄三罪，諸言官及兵部皆請逮鐘。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Qu Shen and others impeached Zhong on three counts of deception; all remonstrance officials and the Ministry of War asked to arrest Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Qu Shen and others charged Zhong with three counts of fraud; remonstrance officials and the Ministry of War alike demanded his arrest.

sentences.zh: 帝以鐘為國繕邊，不當罪，停俸三月。

translations.literal: The emperor considered that Zhong had repaired the border for the state and should not be punished; his salary was suspended for three months.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held that Zhong had fortified the frontier for the realm and ought not be punished; his salary was withheld for three months.

sentences.zh: 正德元年，由巡撫貴州召督漕運兼巡撫江北。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengde he was recalled from Grand Coordinator of Guizhou to supervise grain transport and serve as Grand Coordinator of the region north of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde 1 he was recalled from Guizhou to take charge of the grain transport and serve as grand coordinator of the lower Yangzi north bank.

sentences.zh: 明年就進右都御史。

translations.literal: The next year he was immediately advanced to Censor-in-chief of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted on the spot to censor-in-chief of the right.

sentences.zh: 蘇、松、浙江運舟由下港口及孟瀆河溯大江以達瓜洲，遠涉二百八十餘里，往往遭風濤。

translations.literal: Transport boats of Suzhou, Songjiang, and Zhejiang from Lower Harbor and the Mengdu River went upstream on the Great River to reach Guazhou, involving more than two hundred eighty li and often meeting wind and waves.
translations.idiomatic: Grain barges from Suzhou, Songjiang, and Zhejiang had to ascend the Yangzi from Lower Harbor and the Mengdu River to Guazhou—a run of more than two hundred eighty li, often battered by wind and tide.

sentences.zh: 鐘言：「孟瀆對江有夾河，可抵白塔河口。

translations.literal: Zhong said: "Opposite Mengdu on the river there is a forked channel that can reach the mouth of the Baita River.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong proposed: "Across from Mengdu a parallel channel could reach the mouth of the Baita River.

sentences.zh: 舊置四閘，徑四十里。

translations.literal: Formerly four sluices were placed, a straight distance of forty li.
translations.idiomatic: Four locks along that route would shorten the haul to forty li.

sentences.zh: 至宜陵鎮再折而北，即抵揚州運河。

translations.literal: Reaching Yiling Town and turning north again, one would then reach the Yangzhou canal.
translations.idiomatic: From Yiling Town a bend north would join the Yangzhou canal directly.

sentences.zh: 開浚為便。

translations.literal: Dredging and opening it would be convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Dredging it would be the simpler course.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: " The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 改掌南京都察院，就遷刑部尚書。

translations.literal: He was changed to head the Nanjing Censorate and was immediately transferred to Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned to head the Nanjing Censorate and soon after made minister of punishments.

sentences.zh: 四年冬，加太子少保兼左都御史，掌院事。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourth year he was given the additional titles Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Censor-in-chief of the Left, directing the court's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fourth year he was made junior guardian of the heir apparent and censor-in-chief of the left, with charge of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 五年春，湖廣歲饑盜起。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifth year Huguang suffered famine in the year and bandits rose.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fifth year famine struck Huguang and bandits rose.

sentences.zh: 命鐘以本官總制軍務，陜西、河南、四川亦隸焉。

translations.literal: Zhong was ordered with his present rank to overall military affairs; Shaanxi, Henan, and Sichuan were also placed under him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong was ordered to take overall military command in his existing rank, with Shaanxi, Henan, and Sichuan placed under him as well.

sentences.zh: 沔陽賊楊清、丘仁等僭稱天王、將軍，出沒洞庭間。

translations.literal: The bandits of Mianyang, Yang Qing, Qiu Ren, and others presumptuously styled themselves Heavenly King and General, appearing and disappearing around Dongting.
translations.idiomatic: At Mianyang, Yang Qing, Qiu Ren, and their fellows styled themselves Heavenly King and General and ranged the Dongting region.

sentences.zh: 圍岳州，陷臨湘，官軍屢失利。

translations.literal: They besieged Yuezhou, captured Linxiang, and government troops repeatedly suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: They besieged Yuezhou, took Linxiang, and government forces suffered defeat after defeat.

sentences.zh: 鐘及總兵官毛倫檄都指揮潘勛、柴奎，布政使陳鎬，副使蔣昇擊破之於麻穰灘，擒斬七百四十余人，賊遂平。

translations.literal: Zhong and the commander-in-chief Mao Lun ordered Regional Commanders Pan Xun and Chai Kui, Administration Commissioner Chen Hao, and Vice Commissioner Jiang Sheng to defeat them at Mayang Beach; they captured and killed more than seven hundred forty persons, and the bandits were then pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong and Commander Mao Lun ordered regional commanders Pan Xun and Chai Kui, administration commissioner Chen Hao, and vice commissioner Jiang Sheng to crush them at Mayang Beach; more than seven hundred forty were killed or captured, and the rebellion collapsed.

sentences.zh: 初，鐘掌院事，劉瑾方熾。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhong directed the court's affairs, Liu Jin was at the height of his power.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhong first headed the Censorate, Liu Jin's power was at its height.

sentences.zh: 及瑾誅，言官劾鐘徇瑾撻御史。

translations.literal: When Jin was executed, remonstrance officials impeached Zhong for currying favor with Jin and beating censors.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin's fall, remonstrance officials accused Zhong of pandering to him and having censors flogged.

sentences.zh: 朝議以鐘討賊，置不問。

translations.literal: Court discussion held that because Zhong was suppressing bandits, the matter was set aside without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion held that with Zhong still campaigning against bandits, the charges were set aside.

sentences.zh: 時保寧賊藍廷瑞自稱順天王，鄢本恕自稱「刮地王」，其黨廖惠稱「掃地王」，眾十萬余，置四十八總管，延蔓陜西、湖廣之境。

translations.literal: At that time the Baoning bandit Lan Tingrui styled himself Shuntian King, Yan Benshu styled himself "Land-Scraping King," and his associate Liao Hui styled himself "Ground-Sweeping King"; their forces numbered more than a hundred thousand, with forty-eight commanders appointed, spreading through the territories of Shaanxi and Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile at Baoning, Lan Tingrui styled himself King Who Follows Heaven; Yan Benshu took the title Land-Scraping King; his lieutenant Liao Hui called himself Ground-Sweeping King. Their host exceeded a hundred thousand men under forty-eight commanders, and the revolt spread across Shaanxi and Huguang.

sentences.zh: 廷瑞與惠謀據保寧，本恕謀據漢中，取鄖陽，由荊、襄東下。

translations.literal: Tingrui and Hui plotted to hold Baoning; Benshu plotted to hold Hanzhong, take Yunyang, and go east through Jing and Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Tingrui and Hui aimed to hold Baoning; Benshu planned to seize Hanzhong and Yunyang and drive east through Jing and Xiang.

sentences.zh: 巡撫林俊方議遏通江，而惠已至，攻陷其城，殺參議黃瓚，僉事錢朝鳳等遁去。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Lin Jun was just discussing blocking Tongjiang, but Hui had already arrived, attacked and took its city, killed Participating Secretary Huang Zan, and Assistant Commissioner Qian Chaofeng and others fled.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Lin Jun was still debating how to block Tongjiang when Hui arrived, stormed the city, killed participating secretary Huang Zan, and drove assistant commissioner Qian Chaofeng and others to flight.

sentences.zh: 適官軍自他郡還，賊疑援兵至，亦遁。

translations.literal: It happened that government troops were returning from another prefecture; the bandits suspected reinforcements had arrived and also fled.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops happened to be returning from a neighboring commandery; the rebels took them for reinforcements and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 俊益發羅、回及石矽士兵助朝鳳進剿，參議公勉仁亦會。

translations.literal: Jun further sent Luo, Hui, and Shixi native soldiers to assist Chaofeng in advancing to suppress them; Participating Secretary Gong Mianren also joined.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Jun sent more Luo, Hui, and Shixi native troops to reinforce Qian Chaofeng's pursuit; participating secretary Gong Mianren joined the campaign.

sentences.zh: 龍灘河漲，賊半渡，羅、回奮擊之，擒斬八百余人，墜崖溺水甚眾。

translations.literal: The Longtan River rose; the bandits were half across; the Luo and Hui troops fiercely attacked them, capturing and killing more than eight hundred persons, and very many fell from cliffs and drowned.
translations.idiomatic: At the swollen Longtan River the rebels were caught mid-crossing; Luo and Hui troops struck hard, killing or capturing more than eight hundred, while many more plunged from the cliffs and drowned.

sentences.zh: 俊復遣知府張敏、何珊等追之，獲惠，余眾奔陜西西鄉。

translations.literal: Jun again sent Prefects Zhang Min and He Shan and others to pursue them; Hui was captured, and the remaining masses fled to Xixiang in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Jun sent prefects Zhang Min and He Shan in pursuit; Liao Hui was taken, and the remnant fled into Xixiang, Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 鐘乃下令招撫，歸者萬余人。

translations.literal: Zhong then ordered recruitment and appeasement; more than ten thousand returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong then proclaimed an offer of amnesty; more than ten thousand came in.

sentences.zh: 既而賊收散亡，陷營山，殺僉事王源，縱掠蓬、劍二州。

translations.literal: Before long the bandits gathered the scattered and lost, took Yingshan, killed Assistant Commissioner Wang Yuan, and let their plundering run through the two prefectures of Peng and Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the rebels regrouped, seized Yingshan, killed assistant commissioner Wang Yuan, and ravaged Peng and Jian prefectures.

sentences.zh: 鐘赴四川，與俊議多不合，軍機牽制，賊益熾。

translations.literal: Zhong went to Sichuan; he and Jun disagreed on many points; military affairs were constrained, and the bandits grew fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong entered Sichuan, but he and Lin Jun rarely agreed; operations bogged down, and the rebellion burned hotter.

sentences.zh: 已，乃檄陜西、湖廣、河南兵分道進，湖廣兵先追及於陜西石泉。

translations.literal: Thereafter he ordered troops of Shaanxi, Huguang, and Henan to advance by separate routes; Huguang troops first caught up with them at Shiquan in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Shaanxi, Huguang, and Henan forces forward on separate routes; the Huguang column first caught the rebels at Shiquan in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 廷瑞走漢中，都指揮金冕圍之。

translations.literal: Tingrui fled to Hanzhong; Regional Commander Jin Mian surrounded him.
translations.idiomatic: Tingrui fled to Hanzhong, where regional commander Jin Mian hemmed him in.

sentences.zh: 陜西巡撫藍章方駐漢中，廷瑞遣其黨何虎詣章，乞還川就撫。

translations.literal: Shaanxi Grand Coordinator Lan Zhang was just stationed at Hanzhong; Tingrui sent his associate He Hu to Zhang, begging to return to Sichuan and submit to appeasement.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi grand coordinator Lan Zhang was then at Hanzhong; Tingrui sent his lieutenant He Hu to beg leave to return to Sichuan for surrender talks.

sentences.zh: 章以廷瑞本川賊，恐急之必致死，陜且受患，遂令冕護之出境。

translations.literal: Zhang, because Tingrui was originally a Sichuan bandit, feared that pressing him urgently would make him fight to the death and Shaanxi would then suffer harm; he therefore ordered Mian to escort him out of the border.
translations.idiomatic: Lan Zhang reasoned that Tingrui was a Sichuan rebel at heart: drive him too hard and he would fight to the death, with Shaanxi paying the price. He had Jin Mian escort the band out of the province.

sentences.zh: 廷瑞既入川，求降，鐘等令至東鄉聽撫。

translations.literal: After Tingrui had entered Sichuan he sought to surrender; Zhong and others ordered him to come to Dongxiang to hear appeasement.
translations.idiomatic: Once back in Sichuan, Tingrui sued for peace; Zhong ordered him to Dongxiang to negotiate surrender.

sentences.zh: 賊意在緩師，遷延累月，依山結營，要求營山縣或臨江市屯其眾，遣官為質。

translations.literal: The bandits' intent was to slow the army; they delayed for accumulated months, built camps on the mountains, demanded Yingshan County or Linjiang City to station their masses, and sent an official as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels meant only to stall: month after month they entrenched on the hills, demanding Yingshan county or Linjiang city to quarter their forces and an official hostage as surety.

sentences.zh: 鐘令漢中通判羅賢入其營。

translations.literal: Zhong ordered Hanzhong Assistant Prefect Luo Xian to enter their camp.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong sent Hanzhong assistant prefect Luo Xian into the rebel camp.

sentences.zh: 本恕來謁，約既定，會官軍有殺其樵采者，賊復疑懼，遂殺賢，剽如故。

translations.literal: Benshu came to an audience; the agreement was set, but it happened that government troops killed their wood-gatherers; the bandits again grew suspicious and afraid, then killed Xian, and plundered as before.
translations.idiomatic: Benshu came to parley and terms seemed set—until government troops killed rebel foragers. Suspicion returned; the rebels murdered Luo Xian and resumed their raids.

sentences.zh: 官軍為七壘守之，賊不得逸，其黨漸潰。

translations.literal: Government troops made seven fortified camps to guard them; the bandits could not escape, and their party gradually dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Government forces ringed them with seven fortified camps; the rebels could not break out, and their ranks began to melt away.

sentences.zh: 廷瑞以所掠女子詐為己女，結婚於永順土舍彭世麟，冀得間逸去。

translations.literal: Tingrui took a woman he had plundered and falsely presented her as his own daughter, marrying her to Peng Shilin, a native chieftain's household of Yongshun, hoping to gain an interval to flee away.
translations.idiomatic: Tingrui passed off a captive woman as his daughter and married her to Peng Shilin of the Yongshun native office, hoping a wedding feast would buy him a chance to slip away.

sentences.zh: 世麟密白鐘，鐘授方略使圖之。

translations.literal: Shilin secretly informed Zhong; Zhong gave him stratagems to plot it.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Shilin warned Zhong in secret; Zhong gave him a plan to spring the trap.

sentences.zh: 及期，廷瑞、本恕暨其黨王金珠等二十八人鹹來會。

translations.literal: When the day came, Tingrui, Benshu, and their associates Wang Jinzhu and twenty-eight persons in all came to the meeting.
translations.idiomatic: On the appointed day Tingrui, Benshu, Wang Jinzhu, and twenty-six of their chiefs walked into the feast.

sentences.zh: 伏發悉就擒，惟廖麻子得脫。

translations.literal: The ambush sprang and all were captured; only Liao Mazi escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Hidden troops seized them all—only Liao Mazi slipped the net.

sentences.zh: 其眾聞變，驚潰渡河。

translations.literal: Their masses heard of the change, startled and scattered, and crossed the river.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing what had happened, the main rebel host panicked, broke, and fled across the river.

sentences.zh: 鐘遣兵追擊，俘斬七百余人，以功進太子太保。

translations.literal: Zhong sent troops to pursue and attack; they captured and killed more than seven hundred persons, and for the merit he was advanced to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong sent pursuers who killed or captured more than seven hundred; for this he was promoted to grand guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 未幾，廖麻子及其黨曹甫掠營山、蓬州。

translations.literal: Before long Liao Mazi and his associate Cao Fu plundered Yingshan and Pengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Liao Mazi and his lieutenant Cao Fu were raiding Yingshan and Pengzhou again.

sentences.zh: 七年，總兵官楊宏，副使張敏、馬昊、何珊等合擊之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the commander-in-chief Yang Hong, Vice Commissioners Zhang Min, Ma Hao, He Shan, and others jointly attacked them.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year commander Yang Hong, vice commissioners Zhang Min, Ma Hao, and He Shan, and others combined against them.

sentences.zh: 賊勢蹙，鐘乃議招撫。

translations.literal: The bandit situation was pressed; Zhong then discussed recruitment and appeasement.
translations.idiomatic: With the rebels cornered, Zhong turned again to offers of amnesty.

sentences.zh: 敏以單騎詣甫營，甫聽命，遂赴軍門受約束，歸散其黨。

translations.literal: Min with a single horse went to Fu's camp; Fu obeyed the order, then came to the army gate to accept restraint, returned, and dispersed his party.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Min rode alone into Cao Fu's camp; Fu submitted, came to army headquarters to accept terms, and went home to disband his followers.

sentences.zh: 而麻子忿甫背己，殺之，並其眾，轉掠川東。

translations.literal: But Mazi resented that Fu had betrayed him, killed him and absorbed his forces, and turned to plunder eastern Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liao Mazi, furious at Cao Fu's defection, killed him, absorbed his band, and swept eastern Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 官軍不敢擊，潛躡賊後，馘良民為功，土兵虐尤甚。

translations.literal: Government troops dared not attack; they secretly trailed behind the bandits and claimed common people's ears as merit; native troops abused even more severely.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops would not close with the rebels; they shadowed the rear and tallied peasants' ears as kills, while native auxiliaries preyed on the people worst of all.

sentences.zh: 時有謠曰：「賊如梳，軍如篦，土兵如剃。

translations.literal: At the time there was a rhyme that said: "Bandits are like a comb, the army like a fine-tooth comb, native troops like shaving.
translations.idiomatic: A popular rhyme ran: "The bandits comb you over; the army fine-combs you; the native troops shave you clean.

sentences.zh: 」巡按御史王綸、紀功御史汪景芳劾鐘縱兵不戢。

translations.literal: " Investigating Censor Wang Lun and Merit-recording Censor Wang Jingfang impeached Zhong for indulging troops without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: " Investigating censor Wang Lun and merit-recording censor Wang Jingfang impeached Zhong for letting his troops run wild.

sentences.zh: 綸復奏鐘樂飲縱遊，致賊自合州渡江陷州縣。

translations.literal: Lun again memorialized that Zhong delighted in drink and roaming freely, causing bandits to cross the river from Hezhou and seize prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lun added that Zhong spent his days feasting and touring while rebels crossed from Hezhou and overran one county seat after another.

sentences.zh: 詔召鐘還，以彭澤代，鐘遂乞歸。

translations.literal: An edict recalled Zhong; Peng Ze replaced him, and Zhong then begged to retire.
translations.idiomatic: The throne recalled Zhong; Peng Ze took his post, and Zhong petitioned to retire.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三年卒，謚襄惠。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiajing he died; his posthumous title was Xianghui.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Jiajing 3 and was posthumously titled Xianghui, Beneficent and Assisting.

sentences.zh: 陳鎬，會稽人。

translations.literal: Chen Hao was a man of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hao came from Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 成化二十三年進士。

translations.literal: He was a metropolitan graduate of the twenty-third year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi in Chenghua 23.

sentences.zh: 既平賊，就遷右副都御史，巡撫湖廣。

translations.literal: After the bandits were pacified he was immediately transferred to Vice Censor-in-chief of the Right and made Grand Coordinator of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Once the rebellion was crushed he was promoted on the spot to vice censor-in-chief of the right and appointed grand coordinator of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 蔣昇，祁陽人，鎬同年進士。

translations.literal: Jiang Sheng was a man of Qiyang and a metropolitan graduate of the same year as Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Sheng, of Qiyang, had taken the jinshi in the same year as Chen Hao.

sentences.zh: 陳金，字汝礪，應城人，徙武昌。

translations.literal: Chen Jin, style name Ruli, was a man of Yingcheng who moved to Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jin, styled Ruli, was born in Yingcheng but later settled in Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 祖坦，夔州知府。

translations.literal: His grandfather Tan was prefect of Kuizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Chen Tan had served as prefect of Kuizhou.

sentences.zh: 父琳，廣西僉事。

translations.literal: His father Lin was an assistant commissioner in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chen Lin had been an assistant commissioner in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 金舉成化八年進士，除婺源知縣，擢南京御史。

translations.literal: Jin passed the metropolitan examination in the eighth year of Chenghua, was appointed magistrate of Wuyuan, and was promoted to Nanjing censor.
translations.idiomatic: Jin passed the jinshi in Chenghua 8, served as magistrate of Wuyuan, and was raised to censor at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 弘治初，出按浙江，還因災異劾文武大僚十九人，侍郎丁永中、南京大理卿吳道宏、南寧伯毛文等多罷去。

translations.literal: Early in Hongzhi he went out to inspect Zhejiang; on return, because of disasters and omens he impeached nineteen civil and military grandees; Vice Minister Ding Yongzhong, Nanjing Grand Court Justice Wu Daohong, Nanning Earl Mao Wen, and many others were mostly dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Hongzhi he toured Zhejiang as investigating censor; returning, he used omens and natural disasters to impeach nineteen senior civil and military officials—among them vice minister Ding Yongzhong, Nanjing grand court justice Wu Daohong, and Nanning earl Mao Wen, most of whom were removed.

sentences.zh: 尋遷山西副使，歷雲南左布政使，討平竹子箐叛苗。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Shanxi vice commissioner, served as Yunnan left administration commissioner, and suppressed the rebellious Miao of Zhuziqing.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Shanxi vice commissioner, then Yunnan left administration commissioner, and put down the Miao revolt at Bamboo Gorge.

sentences.zh: 十三年，就拜右副都御史，巡撫其地。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was immediately enfeoffed as Vice Censor-in-chief of the Right and made Grand Coordinator of that region.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was appointed on the spot vice censor-in-chief of the right and grand coordinator of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 孟養酋思祿與孟密酋思揲構兵積年。

translations.literal: The chief of Mengyang, Si Lu, and the chief of Mengmi, Si Ye, had raised arms against each other for accumulated years.
translations.idiomatic: Mengyang chief Si Lu and Mengmi chief Si Ye had been at war for years.

sentences.zh: 金奉詔發緬甸、幹崖、隴川、南甸諸部兵，聚糧十二萬，為征討計，而遣參議郭緒往撫之。

translations.literal: Jin by imperial order raised troops of Burma, Ganya, Longchuan, Nandian, and other departments, gathered one hundred twenty thousand dan of grain, made plans for a punitive campaign, and sent Participating Secretary Guo Xu to appease them.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order Jin mobilized forces from Burma, Ganya, Longchuan, Nandian, and neighboring domains, stockpiled a hundred twenty thousand dan of grain for a full campaign, and dispatched participating secretary Guo Xu to negotiate.

sentences.zh: 思祿懼，遂罷兵修貢，金以功賚銀幣。

translations.literal: Si Lu was afraid, then ceased troops and repaired tribute; Jin for the merit was rewarded with silver and silks.
translations.idiomatic: Si Lu took fright, stood down, and restored tribute; Jin was rewarded with silver and silks for the settlement.

sentences.zh: 貴州兵敗賊婦米魯，米魯退攻平夷衛及大河、扼勒諸堡。

translations.literal: Guizhou troops were defeated by the bandit woman Milu; Milu withdrew to attack Pingyi Guard and the forts of Dahe, Ele, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Guizhou troops were beaten by the bandit leader Milu; she then turned on Pingyi Guard and the outposts at Dahe, Ele, and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 金發兵連破之，增俸一等，召為南京戶部右侍郎。

translations.literal: Jin sent troops in succession to defeat them, increased his salary by one grade, and was summoned as Nanjing Vice Minister of the Right of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Jin sent columns that broke her in successive battles; his salary was raised one grade and he was summoned to Nanjing as vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 正德改元，給事中周璽等劾不職大臣，金與焉。

translations.literal: At the change of reign to Zhengde, Supervising Secretary Zhou Xi and others impeached incompetent grand ministers; Jin was among them.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhengde began, supervising secretary Zhou Xi and others impeached negligent senior ministers—and Jin was named among them.

sentences.zh: 詔不問。

translations.literal: An edict ordered no inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered the charges dropped.

sentences.zh: 金以母老乞歸，不允。

translations.literal: Jin because his mother was old begged to return home; it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Jin pleaded to retire on account of his aged mother; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 尋以右都御史總督兩廣軍務。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Censor-in-chief of the Right to overall the military affairs of the Two Guangs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made censor-in-chief of the right with overall command of military affairs in Guangdong and Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 時內臣韋霦等建議，請輸兩廣各司所貯銀於京師。

translations.literal: At that time the inner eunuch Wei Yu and others proposed to transport the silver stored by the various departments of the Two Guangs to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The palace eunuch Wei Yu and others then proposed shipping all silver held in the Two Guangs to the capital.

sentences.zh: 金疏不可，詔留二十余萬。

translations.literal: Jin memorialized that it could not be done; an edict ordered more than two hundred thousand to be retained.
translations.idiomatic: Jin memorialized against the move; the court agreed to leave more than two hundred thousand taels in place.

sentences.zh: 馬平、洛容僮猖獗，金偕總兵官毛銳發兵十三萬征之，俘斬七千余人，進左都御史。

translations.literal: The Zhuang of Maping and Luorong were fierce; Jin together with Commander Mao Rui sent one hundred thirty thousand troops to campaign against them, capturing and killing more than seven thousand persons, and was advanced to Censor-in-chief of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang rebels at Maping and Luorong were raging; Jin and commander Mao Rui fielded a hundred thirty thousand men, killed or captured more than seven thousand, and Jin was promoted to censor-in-chief of the left.

sentences.zh: 斷藤峽苗時出剽。

translations.literal: The Miao of Duanteng Gorge often came out to plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Miao bands from Duanteng Gorge raided the lowlands whenever they could.

sentences.zh: 金念苗嗜魚鹽，可以利縻也，乃立約束，令民與苗市，改峽曰永通。

translations.literal: Jin reflected that the Miao loved fish and salt and could be bound by profit; he therefore established regulations, ordered the people to market with the Miao, and changed the gorge's name to Yongtong.
translations.idiomatic: Jin reasoned that the Miao craved fish and salt and might be tethered by trade: he set market rules, opened trade between settlers and tribesmen, and renamed the gorge Forever Open.

sentences.zh: 苗性貪而黠，初陽受約，既乃不予直，殺掠益甚。

translations.literal: The Miao nature was greedy and cunning; at first they outwardly accepted the agreement, but thereafter they would not give fair payment, and killing and plundering grew even worse.
translations.idiomatic: Greedy and shrewd, the Miao at first accepted the bargain in name only, then refused fair payment and raided all the harder.

sentences.zh: 潯州人為語曰：「永通不通，來葬江中，誰其作者？

translations.literal: The people of Xunzhou made a saying: "Yongtong does not open; come bury in the middle of the river—who is its maker?
translations.idiomatic: People of Xunzhou composed a verse: "Forever Open stays shut—come be buried mid-river. Who wrought this?

sentences.zh: 噫，陳公！

translations.literal: Alas, Lord Chen!
translations.idiomatic: Alas—Commissioner Chen!

sentences.zh: 」蓋咎金失計也。

translations.literal: " Thus blaming Jin for a failed plan.
translations.idiomatic: "—a bitter verdict on Chen Jin's miscalculation.

sentences.zh: 三年十月，遷南京戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the third year he was transferred to Minister of Revenue at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the third year he was made minister of revenue at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，召為左都御史，未聞命，以母喪歸。

translations.literal: The next winter he was summoned as Censor-in-chief of the Left; before he received the appointment he returned home for his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The following winter he was recalled to be censor-in-chief of the left, but went home for his mother's funeral before the order reached him.

sentences.zh: 六年二月，江西盜起。

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixth year bandits rose in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the sixth year rebels broke out across Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 詔起金故官，總制軍務。

translations.literal: An edict recalled Jin to his former office to overall military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored Jin to his former rank with overall military command.

sentences.zh: 南畿、浙江、福建、廣東、湖廣文武將吏俱隸焉。

translations.literal: Civil and military officers and generals of the Southern Capital Region, Zhejiang, Fujian, Guangdong, and Huguang were all placed under him.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials of the southern capital region, Zhejiang, Fujian, Guangdong, and Huguang all fell under his command.

sentences.zh: 許便宜從事，都指揮以下不用命者專刑戮。

translations.literal: He was permitted to act as circumstances required; regional commanders and below who disobeyed orders could be executed on his sole authority.
translations.idiomatic: He was authorized to act at discretion and to execute regional commanders and subordinates who defied orders.

sentences.zh: 當是時，撫州則東鄉賊王鈺五、徐仰三、傅傑一、揭端三等；

translations.literal: At that time in Fuzhou there were the Dongxiang bandits Wang Yuwu, Xu Yangsan, Fu Jieyi, Jie Duan, and others;
translations.idiomatic: At that time Fuzhou had the Dongxiang rebels Wang Yuwu, Xu Yangsan, Fu Jieyi, Jie Duan, and others;

sentences.zh: 南昌則姚源賊汪澄二、王浩八、殷勇十、洪瑞七等；

translations.literal: in Nanchang the Yaoyuan bandits Wang Chenger, Wang Haoba, Yin Yongshi, Hong Ruiqi, and others;
translations.idiomatic: at Nanchang the Yaoyuan rebels Wang Chenger, Wang Haoba, Yin Yongshi, Hong Ruiqi, and others;

sentences.zh: 瑞州則華林賊羅光權、陳福一等；

translations.literal: in Ruizhou the Hualin bandits Luo Guangquan, Chen Fuyi, and others;
translations.idiomatic: at Ruizhou the Hualin rebels Luo Guangquan, Chen Fuyi, and others;

sentences.zh: 而贛州大帽山賊何積欽等又起。

translations.literal: and at Ganzhou the Damaoshan bandits He Jiqin and others also rose.
translations.idiomatic: while at Ganzhou the Damao Mountain rebels He Jiqin and others rose as well.

sentences.zh: 官軍累年不能克。

translations.literal: Government troops for years could not overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: Government forces had failed to crush them for years.

sentences.zh: 金以屬郡兵不足用，奏調廣西狼土兵。

translations.literal: Jin, because the troops of the subordinate prefectures were insufficient, memorialized to transfer Guangxi wolf-and-native troops.
translations.idiomatic: Finding local garrisons inadequate, Jin memorialized for Guangxi wolf troops and native auxiliaries.

sentences.zh: 明年二月先進兵東鄉，遣參議徐蕃等分屯要害，而令副總兵張勇，土官岑瑽、岑猛各統官兵、目兵擊賊熟塘。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year he advanced first on Dongxiang, sent Participating Secretary Xu Fan and others to garrison key points separately, and ordered Vice Commander-in-chief Zhang Yong and native officials Cen Cong and Cen Meng each to command government troops and native soldiers to strike the bandits at Shutang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the next year he opened with an advance on Dongxiang, posted participating secretary Xu Fan and others at choke points, and ordered vice commander Zhang Yong and native chiefs Cen Cong and Cen Meng to lead regular and tribal troops against the rebels at Shutang.

sentences.zh: 進戰南甗，追敗之赤岸蔭嶺。

translations.literal: Advancing to battle at Nanyong, he pursued and defeated them at Chian and Yinling.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing south to Nanyong, he drove them in defeat to Chian and Yinling.

sentences.zh: 擒仰三，馘鈺五等，克柵二百六十五，斬首萬一千六百余級，俘七百五十余人。

translations.literal: Yangsan was captured; Yuwu and others were beheaded; two hundred sixty-five stockades were taken; heads numbered more than eleven thousand six hundred; more than seven hundred fifty were captured alive.
translations.idiomatic: They took Yangsan alive, beheaded Yuwu and his fellows, stormed two hundred sixty-five stockades, counted more than eleven thousand six hundred heads, and captured over seven hundred fifty men.

sentences.zh: 五月移師姚源，令參政董樸、吳廷舉等分營余幹、安仁、貴溪、鄱陽、樂平遏賊，而親統大軍搗其巢，勇十重創死。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he shifted his army to Yaoyuan, ordered Administration Commissioners Dong Pu and Wu Tingju and others to camp separately at Yugan, Anren, Guixi, Poyang, and Leping to block the bandits, while he personally commanded the main force to storm their lair; Yongshi died of severe wounds.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he moved on Yaoyuan, sent administration commissioners Dong Pu and Wu Tingju to block escape routes through Yugan, Anren, Guixi, Poyang, and Leping, and led the main column against the nest himself; Yin Yongshi died of his wounds.

sentences.zh: 會張勇以目兵至，毒弩射殺瑞七、成七等，俘斬共五千余人。

translations.literal: It happened that Zhang Yong arrived with native troops; poisoned crossbows shot and killed Ruiqi, Chengqi, and others; captures and kills together exceeded five thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yong then arrived with native troops; poisoned bolts killed Ruiqi, Chengqi, and others; kills and captures together exceeded five thousand.

sentences.zh: 七月乘勝斬光權。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, riding the victory, Guangquan was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he pressed the advantage and beheaded Luo Guangquan.

sentences.zh: 華林賊盡平。

translations.literal: The Hualin bandits were entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The Hualin rebels were wiped out.

sentences.zh: 又督副使王秩等擊大帽山賊，獲積欽，俘斬千七百余人。

translations.literal: He also supervised Vice Commissioner Wang Zhi and others in attacking the Damaoshan bandits; Jiqin was captured; more than seventeen hundred were captured or killed.
translations.idiomatic: He also directed vice commissioner Wang Zhi against the Damao Mountain rebels, took He Jiqin, and killed or captured more than seventeen hundred.

sentences.zh: 半歲間，剿賊幾盡。

translations.literal: Within half a year the bandits were nearly all exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Within half a year the rebellion was nearly extinguished.

sentences.zh: 遂即東鄉立縣，並立萬年縣，招降人居之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he established a county at Dongxiang and also established Wannian County, settling surrendered people there.
translations.idiomatic: He then founded a county at Dongxiang, created Wannian county, and settled surrendered people there.

sentences.zh: 前後每奏捷，輒賜璽書嘉勞，賚銀幣。

translations.literal: Whenever he reported victory the court would bestow sealed letters of praise and reward silver and silks.
translations.idiomatic: Each victory brought sealed imperial praise and gifts of silver and silks.

sentences.zh: 加太子少保，蔭子錦衣世百戶。

translations.literal: He was given the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and his son was granted hereditary enrollment in the Embroidered Uniform Guard as a commander of one hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was made junior guardian of the heir apparent, and his son received a hereditary command in the Embroidered Uniform Guard at one hundred households.

sentences.zh: 金累破劇賊，然所用目兵貪殘嗜殺，剽掠甚於賊，有巨族數百口闔門罹害者。

translations.literal: Jin repeatedly broke fierce bandits, yet the native soldiers he used were greedy, cruel, and bloodthirsty; their plundering exceeded the bandits', and great clans of several hundred persons suffered entire households wiped out.
translations.idiomatic: Jin broke one fierce rebel band after another, yet the native auxiliaries he employed were greedier and more murderous than the rebels; whole great clans of hundreds perished.

sentences.zh: 所獲婦女率指為賊屬，載數千艘去。

translations.literal: Women they seized were mostly labeled bandit kin and shipped away on thousands of boats.
translations.idiomatic: Captured women were routinely called rebel kin and sent off by the thousand boatloads.

sentences.zh: 民間謠曰：「土賊猶可，土兵殺我。

translations.literal: The people made a rhyme that said: "Native bandits one can still bear; native troops will kill us.
translations.idiomatic: A popular rhyme ran: "Rebel tribesmen you can still endure; government tribesmen will kill you."

sentences.zh: 」金亦知民患之，方倚其力，不為禁。

translations.literal: " Jin also knew the people suffered from them, but as he relied on their strength he did not forbid it.
translations.idiomatic: " Jin knew the people suffered, but because he depended on their strength he did not restrain them.

sentences.zh: 又不能持廉，軍資頗私入。

translations.literal: He also could not remain incorrupt; a fair portion of military funds went into his private purse.
translations.idiomatic: Nor could he stay clean: much of the war chest found its way into his own purse.

sentences.zh: 功雖多，士民皆深怨焉。

translations.literal: Though his achievements were many, officials and commoners alike deeply resented him.
translations.idiomatic: His victories were many, yet officials and commoners alike bitterly resented him.

sentences.zh: 東鄉之役，瑽兵縱弩射，趫捷若飛，賊大窘。

translations.literal: In the Dongxiang campaign Cong's troops loosed crossbows; leaping and swift as flight, they drove the bandits into desperate straits.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dongxiang fighting, Cen Cong's archers shot on the run, swift as birds, and cornered the rebels.

sentences.zh: 鎏兵要賞千金，金靳不予，乃縱賊使逸。

translations.literal: Meng's troops demanded a reward of a thousand taels; Jin refused to grant it, and therefore let the bandits escape.
translations.idiomatic: Cen Meng's men demanded a thousand taels; Jin refused, and they deliberately let the rebels slip away.

sentences.zh: 桀黠者多不死，尚數千人。

translations.literal: The most cunning among them mostly did not die; several thousand still remained.
translations.idiomatic: The craftiest rebels mostly survived; several thousand were still at large.

sentences.zh: 金急欲成功，遂下令招撫。

translations.literal: Jin urgently wished to complete his success and therefore ordered recruitment and appeasement.
translations.idiomatic: Eager to declare victory, Jin ordered another round of amnesty talks.

sentences.zh: 其破姚源賊也，金喜，謂功在旦夕，與將吏置酒高會。

translations.literal: When he broke the Yaoyuan bandits Jin rejoiced, thinking success was within a day or two, and with his generals and officials set up a lofty banquet.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yaoyuan rebels seemed broken, Jin rejoiced, thinking the end was a day or two away, and feasted his officers.

sentences.zh: 賊覘諸要害無守者，乃悉所有賂目兵，乘暮遁去。

translations.literal: The bandits spied that the key points were unguarded; they then used all they had to bribe the native troops and fled at dusk.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels saw the passes unguarded, bribed the native troops with everything they had, and slipped away at dusk.

sentences.zh: 時賊絕爨已三日，自分必死，沿途棄稚弱，散婦女。

translations.literal: At the time the bandits had gone three days without cooking fires and had resigned themselves to death; along the way they abandoned infants and scattered women.
translations.idiomatic: They had gone three days without cooking and expected to die; along the road they abandoned children and cast off women.

sentences.zh: 及抵貴溪，始得一飽食，遂轉掠衢、徽間。

translations.literal: Only when they reached Guixi did they at last get a full meal, then turned to plunder Qizhou and Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Only at Guixi did they eat their fill, then swept through Quzhou and Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 金知失策，亦下令招降。

translations.literal: Jin, knowing he had misjudged, also ordered recruitment and appeasement.
translations.idiomatic: Realizing his blunder, Jin issued another amnesty offer.

sentences.zh: 賊首王浩八等故偽降以緩官兵，攻剽如故，卒不能盡賊。

translations.literal: The bandit chiefs Wang Haoba and others had long feigned surrender to slow the government troops; raiding and plundering continued as before, and in the end the bandits could not be fully eliminated.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel chiefs such as Wang Haoba had long pretended to submit only to stall the army; they raided as before, and the revolt was never fully crushed.

sentences.zh: 紀功給事中黎奭及兩京言官交章劾金。

translations.literal: Merit-recording Supervising Secretary Li Yi and remonstrance officials of both capitals memorialized in succession impeaching Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Merit-recording supervising secretary Li Yi and remonstrance officials in both capitals impeached Jin in turn.

sentences.zh: 乃召金還，以俞諫代。

translations.literal: Jin was then recalled and Yu Jian replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: The court recalled Jin and replaced him with Yu Jian.

sentences.zh: 金遂請終喪去。

translations.literal: Jin then asked to leave office to complete his mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Jin petitioned to retire and finish mourning his mother.

sentences.zh: 十年再起，督兩廣軍務。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was recalled again to overall the military affairs of the Two Guangs.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was recalled again to command military affairs in Guangdong and Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 府江賊王公珣等為亂，金集諸道兵偕總兵官郭勛等分六路討之，斬公珣，大有所俘獲。

translations.literal: The Fujiang bandits Wang Gongxun and others made trouble; Jin gathered troops of all circuits together with Commander Guo Xun and others to attack them on six routes, beheaded Gongxun, and captured a great deal.
translations.idiomatic: The Fujiang rebels Wang Gongxun and others rose; Jin assembled forces from every circuit with commander Guo Xun and others, attacked on six fronts, killed Gongxun, and took many captives.

sentences.zh: 加少保太子太保，蔭子如初。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Junior Guardian and Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent; his son's privilege was as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to junior guardian and grand guardian of the heir apparent; his son's privilege remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 復以饒平捷，詔子先受蔭者進一秩。

translations.literal: Again, because of victory at Raoping, an edict advanced by one rank the son who had earlier received the privilege.
translations.idiomatic: After victory at Raoping, an edict raised by one rank the son who had already received the hereditary privilege.

sentences.zh: 金承召還朝，道得疾歸，詔強起之。

translations.literal: Jin, while returning to court on summons, fell ill on the road and went home; an edict ordered him forcibly recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Called back to court, he fell ill on the road and returned home; the throne ordered him recalled by force.

sentences.zh: 十四年冬入掌都察院事。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourteenth year he entered to direct the affairs of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fourteenth year he took charge of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 世宗立，請老，命乘傳還。

translations.literal: When the Shizong emperor acceded, he asked to retire; he was ordered to return by fast courier.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong acceded, he asked to retire and was sent home by imperial post.

sentences.zh: 久之，卒。

translations.literal: After a long while he died.
translations.idiomatic: Years later he died.

sentences.zh: 俞諫，字良佐，桐廬人。

translations.literal: Yu Jian, style name Liangzuo, was a man of Tonglu.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jian, styled Liangzuo, came from Tonglu.

sentences.zh: 父藎，舉進士，官御史，按江西，治外戚王氏、萬氏宗族恣橫罪。

translations.literal: His father Jin had passed the metropolitan examination, served as a censor, and when inspecting Jiangxi punished the crimes of the consort clans Wang and Wan for arrogant license.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yu Jin had been a jinshi and censor; touring Jiangxi, he punished the Wang and Wan consort clans for riding roughshod over the law.

sentences.zh: 坐事，謫澧州判官。

translations.literal: Because of an affair he was demoted to assistant magistrate of Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later demoted to assistant magistrate of Lizhou over an unrelated case.

sentences.zh: 大築陂堰，溉田可萬頃。

translations.literal: He greatly built dikes and weirs and irrigated fields of up to ten thousand qing.
translations.idiomatic: There he built great dikes and canals and irrigated fields totaling ten thousand qing.

sentences.zh: 累遷鄖陽知府。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to prefect of Yunyang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in due course to prefect of Yunyang.

sentences.zh: 諫舉弘治三年進士，授長清知縣，擢南京御史。

translations.literal: Jian passed the metropolitan examination in the third year of Hongzhi, was appointed magistrate of Changqing, and was promoted to Nanjing censor.
translations.idiomatic: Jian passed the jinshi in Hongzhi 3, served as magistrate of Changqing, and was raised to censor at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 遷河南僉事，擒嵩賊呂梅。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Henan vice commissioner and captured the Song bandit Lü Mei.
translations.idiomatic: As Henan vice commissioner he captured the Song bandit Lü Mei.

sentences.zh: 歷江西參議，平大帽山賊。

translations.literal: He served in succession as Jiangxi participating secretary and pacified the Damaoshan bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Jiangxi participating secretary and pacified the Damao Mountain rebels.

sentences.zh: 遷廣東副使，中道召為大理少卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Guangdong vice commissioner; midway he was summoned as Vice Minister of the Grand Court of Revision.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Guangdong vice commissioner, then summoned en route to be vice minister of the Court of Revision.

sentences.zh: 正德六年擢右僉都御史，治水蘇、杭諸府，修治圩塘，民享其利。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhengde he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-chief, managed waterworks in Suzhou, Hangzhou, and other prefectures, and repaired polder dikes; the people enjoyed the benefit.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde 6 he was made right vice censor-in-chief, oversaw water control in Suzhou, Hangzhou, and neighboring prefectures, repaired polder dikes, and won the people's gratitude.

sentences.zh: 尋進右副都御史，提督操江。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to Right Vice Censor-in-chief and put in charge of drilling the Yangtze defense.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to right vice censor-in-chief with charge of Yangtze defense drills.

sentences.zh: 八年春，姚源降賊王浩八叛，詔以諫代陳金督江西、浙江、福建諸軍討之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eighth year the surrendered Yaoyuan bandit Wang Haoba rebelled; an edict ordered Jian to replace Chen Jin in commanding the armies of Jiangxi, Zhejiang, and Fujian to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eighth year the surrendered Yaoyuan rebel Wang Haoba rose again; Jian was ordered to replace Chen Jin and command Jiangxi, Zhejiang, and Fujian forces against him.

sentences.zh: 時浩八眾萬余，屯浙江開化，為同知伍文定等所敗，遁還江西德興，以所執都指揮白弘、江洪為質，求撫於按察使王秩。

translations.literal: At that time Haoba's masses exceeded ten thousand; they were stationed at Kaihua in Zhejiang and were defeated by Assistant Prefect Wu Wendeng and others; they fled back to Dexing in Jiangxi, took the regional commander Bai Hong and the commander Jiang Hong whom they held as hostages, and sought appeasement from Vice Commissioner Wang Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Haoba then commanded more than ten thousand men at Kaihua, Zhejiang; defeated by assistant prefect Wu Wendeng and others, he fled to Dexing in Jiangxi, held regional commander Bai Hong and commander Jiang Hong hostage, and sued for peace through vice commissioner Wang Zhi.

sentences.zh: 秩受之，為傳送姚源。

translations.literal: Zhi accepted them and had them conveyed to Yaoyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi accepted the hostages and sent them on to Yaoyuan.

sentences.zh: 浩八奔據貴溪裴源山，余眾復集，連營十里。

translations.literal: Haoba fled to occupy Peiyuan Mountain in Guixi; the remaining masses gathered again and linked camps for ten li.
translations.idiomatic: Haoba then seized Peiyuan Mountain in Guixi; remnants regrouped in a ten-li chain of camps.

sentences.zh: 諫令秩與副使胡世寧、參政吳廷舉列屯要害，斷其歸路，而躬與都督李鋐乘夜冒雨潛進。

translations.literal: Jian ordered Zhi, together with Vice Commissioner Hu Shining and Administration Commissioner Wu Tingju, to camp at key points and cut off their retreat, while he himself with the regional commander Li Gang advanced by night through rain in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Jian posted Wang Zhi, Hu Shining, and Wu Tingju at choke points to sever retreat, while he and regional commander Li Gang stole forward through rain by night.

sentences.zh: 大破之，俘斬數千人，遂擒浩八。

translations.literal: They inflicted a great defeat, capturing and killing several thousand; Haoba was then captured.
translations.idiomatic: They won a crushing victory, killing or capturing thousands, and took Haoba.

sentences.zh: 其黨潰走玉山。

translations.literal: Their party scattered and fled to Yushan.
translations.idiomatic: The remnant fled to Yushan.

sentences.zh: 諫與南贛巡撫周南、江西巡撫任漢復擊斬七百余人。

translations.literal: Jian together with Grand Coordinator of Southern Ganzhou Zhou Nan and Grand Coordinator of Jiangxi Ren Han again attacked and killed more than seven hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Jian, with grand coordinators Zhou Nan of southern Ganzhou and Ren Han of Jiangxi, struck again and killed more than seven hundred.

sentences.zh: 余賊奔姚源，諫督廷舉等進剿，逼擒之。

translations.literal: The remaining bandits fled to Yaoyuan; Jian supervised Tingju and others in advancing to suppress them and pressed them until captured.
translations.idiomatic: Survivors ran to Yaoyuan; Jian drove Wu Tingju and others forward until the rebels were cornered and taken.

sentences.zh: 諫懲金失，一意用兵，而任漢懦。

translations.literal: Jian, punishing Jin's failures, was bent wholly on military action, while Ren Han was timid.
translations.idiomatic: Stung by Chen Jin's failures, Jian insisted on force alone; Ren Han was timid.

sentences.zh: 先為布政使，嘗贊金主撫。

translations.literal: Having earlier been an administration commissioner, he had once supported Jin in favoring appeasement.
translations.idiomatic: As a former administration commissioner he had once backed Jin's preference for negotiation.

sentences.zh: 雖亟上首功，追賊緩，余當復起。

translations.literal: Though he urgently reported the first merit, pursuit of the bandits was slow, and the rest would surely rise again.
translations.idiomatic: Though he hurried first credit to the throne, pursuit lagged, and the survivors were sure to revive.

sentences.zh: 先是，東鄉賊為金所敗乞降，隸世寧，號新兵，而剽掠如故。

translations.literal: Earlier the Dongxiang bandits, defeated by Jin, had begged to surrender and were placed under Shining, styled New Troops, yet they plundered as before.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Dongxiang rebels beaten by Jin had surrendered to Hu Shining as "New Troops," yet still raided as before.

sentences.zh: 既懼罪復叛，遣參將桂勇等討擒之。

translations.literal: Fearing punishment they rebelled again; Regional Commander Gui Yong and others were sent to attack and capture them.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing punishment, they rebelled again; regional commander Gui Yong and others were sent to crush them.

sentences.zh: 萬年雖立縣，賊尚眾，吏胥多賊黨，官府動息必知之。

translations.literal: Though Wannian County had been established, bandits were still numerous; clerks and runners were mostly bandit partisans, and the government offices' every move was known to them.
translations.idiomatic: Wannian county existed, but rebels remained numerous; yamen clerks were often rebel spies, and official movements were instantly known.

sentences.zh: 副使李情治峻急，眾欲叛，畏鋐在余幹不敢發。

translations.literal: Vice Commissioner Li Qing governed with harsh severity; the masses wished to rebel but feared Gang's presence at Yugan and dared not act.
translations.idiomatic: Vice commissioner Li Qing ruled harshly; the people meant to rebel but dared not while Li Gang held Yugan.

sentences.zh: 會鋐卒，王垂七、胡念二等遂作亂。

translations.literal: When Gang died, Wang Chuiqi, Hu Nianer, and others then made trouble.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Gang died, Wang Chuiqi, Hu Nianer, and others rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 殺情及饒州通判陳達、秦碧，指揮邢世臣等，焚廨舍。

translations.literal: They killed Qing and Assistant Prefect of Raozhou Chen Da, Qin Bi, Commander Xing Shichen, and others, and burned the government offices.
translations.idiomatic: They killed Li Qing, Raozhou assistant prefect Chen Da and Qin Bi, commander Xing Shichen, and others, and burned the yamen.

sentences.zh: 諫發兵擒之，亂乃定。

translations.literal: Jian sent troops and captured them; the disorder was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Jian sent troops, seized the ringleaders, and the disturbance subsided.

sentences.zh: 言官劾諫及漢、南。

translations.literal: Remonstrance officials impeached Jian together with Han and Nan.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance officials impeached Jian along with Ren Han and Zhou Nan.

sentences.zh: 兵部請召漢還，命諫兼領巡撫。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War asked to recall Han; Jian was ordered to take on the grand coordinator's duties as well.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War urged recalling Ren Han; Jian was ordered to assume the grand coordinator's role as well.

sentences.zh: 明年擊臨川賊，斬其魁，而遣參將李隆擊新淦賊。

translations.literal: The next year he attacked the Linchuan bandits, beheaded their leader, and sent Regional Commander Li Long to strike the Xingan bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he struck Linchuan rebels, killed their chief, and sent regional commander Li Long against Xingan.

sentences.zh: 賊踞萬山中，僭稱王且八年。

translations.literal: The bandits held the depths of the myriad mountains and had presumptuously styled themselves kings for eight years.
translations.idiomatic: They held the deep mountains, had styled themselves kings for eight years.

sentences.zh: 隆等深入，悉就擒，俘斬千七百余人。

translations.literal: Long and others penetrated deeply; all were captured; more than seventeen hundred were captured or killed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Long drove deep into the hills; all were taken; more than seventeen hundred were killed or captured.

sentences.zh: 錄功，進諫右都御史，巡撫如故。

translations.literal: Merit was recorded; Jian was advanced to Censor-in-chief of the Right while remaining grand coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: For the victory Jian was promoted to censor-in-chief of the right while retaining his grand coordinator post.

sentences.zh: 劇賊徐九齡者，初嘯聚建昌、醴源。

translations.literal: The fierce bandit Xu Jiuling had at first gathered at Jianchang and Liyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The formidable rebel Xu Jiuling had first rallied at Jianchang and Liyuan.

sentences.zh: 已，出沒江、湖間，積三十年。

translations.literal: Thereafter he appeared and disappeared between the Yangzi and the lakes for thirty accumulated years.
translations.idiomatic: He then ranged the Yangzi and the lakes for thirty years.

sentences.zh: 黃州、德安、九江、安慶、池州、太平鹹被其害。

translations.literal: Huangzhou, Dean, Jiujiang, Anqing, Chizhou, and Taiping were all harmed by him.
translations.idiomatic: Huangzhou, Dean, Jiujiang, Anqing, Chizhou, and Taiping all suffered at his hands.

sentences.zh: 諫討斬之，群盜悉平。

translations.literal: Jian campaigned against him and beheaded him; all the bandit groups were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Jian campaigned against him, beheaded him, and the remaining outlaw bands collapsed.

sentences.zh: 寧王宸濠諷御史張鰲山劾諫，十一年召還，遂乞致仕。

translations.literal: The Prince of Ning Zhu Chenhao prompted Censor Zhang Aoshan to impeach Jian; in the eleventh year he was recalled and then asked to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Ning Zhu Chenhao prompted censor Zhang Aoshan to impeach Jian; in the eleventh year he was recalled and petitioned to retire.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖改元，用薦起故官，總督漕運。

translations.literal: At the change of reign to Jiajing he was raised on recommendation to his former office and made overall supervisor of grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: At the Jiajing accession he was recommended back to office and put in charge of grain transport.

sentences.zh: 青州礦盜王堂等起顏神鎮，流劫東昌、兗州、濟南。

translations.literal: Qingzhou mine bandits Wang Tang and others rose at Yanshen Town and flowed out to plunder Dongchang, Yanzhou, and Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhou mine rebels Wang Tang and others rose at Yanshen Town and raided Dongchang, Yanzhou, and Jinan.

sentences.zh: 都指揮楊紀及指揮楊浩等擊之，浩死，紀僅免。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Yang Ji and Commander Yang Hao and others attacked them; Hao died and Ji barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Regional commander Yang Ji and commander Yang Hao attacked them; Hao was killed and Ji barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 詔責山東將吏，於是諸臣分道逐賊，賊不復屯聚，流劫金鄉、魚臺間。

translations.literal: An edict blamed the Shandong generals and officials; thereupon the various ministers pursued the bandits by separate routes; the bandits no longer massed in camps but flowed out to plunder between Jinxiang and Yutai.
translations.idiomatic: The throne rebuked Shandong commanders; officials then chased the rebels on separate routes; they ceased massing and raided between Jinxiang and Yutai.

sentences.zh: 突曹州，欲渡河不得，復掠考城並河西岸，至東明、長垣。

translations.literal: They burst into Caozhou, wished to cross the river but could not, and again plundered Kaocheng and the west bank of the river, reaching Dongming and Changyuan.
translations.idiomatic: They struck Caozhou, failed to cross the Yellow River, swept Kaocheng and the west bank, and reached Dongming and Changyuan.

sentences.zh: 河南及保定守臣鹹告急。

translations.literal: The defending officials of Henan and Baoding all reported urgent distress.
translations.idiomatic: Henan and Baoding defenders alike sent desperate alarms.

sentences.zh: 賊黨王友賢等轉掠祥符、封丘，南抵徐州。

translations.literal: The bandit associate Wang Youxian and others turned to plunder Xiangfu and Fengqiu and went south to Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel lieutenant Wang Youxian and others raided Xiangfu and Fengqiu and pushed south to Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 廷議以諸道巡撫權位相埒，乃命諫與都督魯綱並提督兩畿、山東、河南軍務，以便宜節制諸道兵討之。

translations.literal: Court discussion held that the grand coordinators of the various circuits held equal rank; Jian and the regional commander Lu Gang were therefore jointly ordered to overall the military affairs of the Two Capitals, Shandong, and Henan, with discretionary authority to command the troops of the various circuits to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Because grand coordinators of the various circuits held equal rank, Jian and regional commander Lu Gang were jointly ordered to command military affairs in the two capitals regions, Shandong, and Henan, with discretionary power over all circuit troops.

sentences.zh: 賊復流至考城。

translations.literal: The bandits again flowed to Kaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels once more swept into Kaocheng.

sentences.zh: 官軍方欲擊，而河南降賊張進引三百騎馳至。

translations.literal: The government troops were just about to strike when the Henan surrendered bandit Zhang Jin led three hundred horsemen in a gallop to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Government forces were about to attack when Zhang Jin, a surrendered rebel from Henan, raced up with three hundred cavalry.

sentences.zh: 中都留守顏愷與俱前，方戰，進忽三麾其旗先卻。

translations.literal: The Central Capital commandant Yan Kai advanced together with them; just as they fought, Jin suddenly waved his banner three times and first withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Central Capital commandant Yan Kai advanced with him; mid-battle Zhang Jin thrice waved his banner and pulled back first.

sentences.zh: 賊乘之，官軍大潰，將士死者八百余人。

translations.literal: The bandits seized the opportunity; the government army suffered great rout; more than eight hundred officers and soldiers died.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels pressed the advantage; government troops collapsed; more than eight hundred officers and men fell.

sentences.zh: 諫等連營進，賊始滅。

translations.literal: Jian and others advanced with linked camps; only then were the bandits extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Jian advanced camp by camp until the rebels were finally destroyed.

sentences.zh: 其秋，召掌都察院事。

translations.literal: That autumn, he was summoned to preside over the affairs of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he was called to head the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 逾年卒官，贈太子太保，謚莊襄。

translations.literal: After more than a year he died in office; posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent; posthumous title Zhuangxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office the following year and was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous name Zhuangxiang.

sentences.zh: 周南，字文化，縉雲人。

translations.literal: Zhou Nan, style name Wenhua, a native of Jinyun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Nan, styled Wenhua, was from Jinyun.

sentences.zh: 成化十四年進士。

translations.literal: Graduate of the jinshi degree in the fourteenth year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fourteenth year of Chenghua.

sentences.zh: 除六合知縣，擢御史，出按畿輔。

translations.literal: Appointed magistrate of Luhe, promoted to investigating censor, sent out to inspect the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Luhe, was promoted to censor, and toured the capital districts.

sentences.zh: 弘治初，再按廣東，劾總兵官柳景。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongzhi, he again inspected Guangdong and impeached the regional commander Liu Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Hongzhi he inspected Guangdong a second time and impeached regional commander Liu Jing.

sentences.zh: 歷江西右布政使，擢右副都御史，巡撫大同。

translations.literal: He passed through the posts of Right Provincial Administration Commissioner of Jiangxi, was promoted to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief, and grand-coordinated Datong.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through Jiangxi administration to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Datong.

sentences.zh: 武宗初立，寇入宣府，參將陳雄等邀擊，敗之。

translations.literal: When Wuzong first ascended, invaders entered Xuanfu; Assistant Commander Chen Xiong and others intercepted and struck them and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzong took the throne, raiders entered Xuanfu; assistant commander Chen Xiong and others intercepted and routed them.

sentences.zh: 錄功，增南俸一秩，母喪歸。

translations.literal: His merit was recorded; Nan's salary was increased one grade; he returned on his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: For this exploit Nan's stipend rose one rank; he then went home for his mother's mourning.

sentences.zh: 正德三年，劉瑾擅政，以大同倉粟有浥爛者，逮南及督糧郎中孫祿下詔獄，械送大同，責倍輸。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhengde, Liu Jin monopolized government; because there was grain in the Datong granary that was soaked and rotten, Nan and Grain Supervising Director Sun Lu were seized and sent to the prison of the imperial command, shackled and escorted to Datong, and charged to pay double delivery.
