translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhengde Liu Jin dominated the court; spoiled grain was found in Datong's granary, and Nan with supervising director Sun Lu were thrown into the imperial prison, sent in chains to Datong, and ordered to make double restitution.

sentences.zh: 會赦，大同總兵官葉椿等為請，免其倍數。

translations.literal: It happened that there was an amnesty; Datong regional commander Ye Chun and others pleaded on their behalf, and their double payment was remitted.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty followed; regional commander Ye Chun interceded, and the double levy was waived.

sentences.zh: 輸畢，釋為民。

translations.literal: When payment was finished, they were released as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: After they paid in full they were released as civilians.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，以故官撫宣府不就，引病歸。

translations.literal: When Jin was executed, he was offered his former office to grand-coordinate Xuanfu but did not accept and cited illness to return home.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin's execution he was offered his old post at Xuanfu but declined and retired citing illness.

sentences.zh: 明年起督南、贛軍務。

translations.literal: The next year he was raised to supervise the military affairs of Nan and Gan.
translations.idiomatic: Next year he was recalled to supervise military affairs in southern Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 南贛巡撫之設，自南始。

translations.literal: The establishment of the Nan-Gan grand coordinator post began with Nan.
translations.idiomatic: The office of Nan-Gan grand coordinator was created for him.

sentences.zh: 汀州大帽山賊張時旺、黃鏞、劉隆、李四仔等聚眾稱王，攻剽城邑，延及江西、廣東之境，數年不靖，官軍討之輒敗。

translations.literal: At Damao Mountain in Tingzhou the bandits Zhang Shiwang, Huang Yong, Liu Long, Li Sizai, and others gathered masses, styled themselves kings, attacked and plundered towns, extended into the territories of Jiangxi and Guangdong, and for several years were not pacified; whenever government troops campaigned against them they were regularly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: On Damao Mountain in Tingzhou, Zhang Shiwang, Huang Yong, Liu Long, Li Sizai, and others gathered bands, proclaimed themselves kings, raided towns across Jiangxi and Guangdong for years, and repeatedly crushed government expeditions.

sentences.zh: 推官莫仲昭、知縣蔣璣、指揮楊澤等被執，賊勢愈熾。

translations.literal: Pushuan Mo Zhongzhao, magistrate Jiang Ji, commander Yang Ze, and others were seized; the bandit momentum grew ever fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy magistrate Mo Zhongzhao, magistrate Jiang Ji, commander Yang Ze, and others were captured, and rebel power surged.

sentences.zh: 南集諸道兵擊之龍牙，擒時旺。

translations.literal: Nan assembled troops from the various circuits and struck them at Longya and captured Shiwang.
translations.idiomatic: Nan gathered troops from every circuit, struck at Longya, and captured Shiwang.

sentences.zh: 義民林富別擊斬鏞於鐵坑。

translations.literal: The righteous commoner Lin Fu separately struck and beheaded Yong at Tiekeng.
translations.idiomatic: Militiaman Lin Fu separately attacked and killed Yong at Iron Pit.

sentences.zh: 其他諸寨為指揮孫堂等所破。

translations.literal: The other stockades were broken by Commander Sun Tang and others.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Sun Tang and others destroyed the remaining strongholds.

sentences.zh: 而副使楊璋、僉事淩相等亦擊隆、四仔，擒之。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Vice Commissioner Yang Zhang, Prefectural Judge Ling Xiang, and others also struck Long and Sizai and captured them.
translations.idiomatic: Vice commissioner Yang Zhang and prefectural judge Ling Xiang also struck Liu Long and Li Sizai and took them.

sentences.zh: 先後斬獲五千人，仲昭等得逸還。

translations.literal: In succession more than five thousand were beheaded or captured; Zhongzhao and others obtained release and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Government forces killed or captured five thousand in all; Zhongzhao and the other captives were freed.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，賜敕獎勞。

translations.literal: When the victory was reported, an imperial letter was bestowed to reward and console.
translations.idiomatic: Upon news of victory the throne sent a patent of commendation.

sentences.zh: 南乃移師會總督陳金，共平姚源諸賊，境內遂寧。

translations.literal: Nan thereupon moved his army to join Grand Coordinator Chen Jin and together pacified the bandits of Yaoyuan and the like; within the borders thereupon was peace.
translations.idiomatic: Nan then joined grand coordinator Chen Jin to pacify the Yaoyuan rebels, and the region was finally quiet.

sentences.zh: 九年春，進右都御史，總督兩廣軍務。

translations.literal: In the spring of the ninth year he was advanced to Right Censor-in-Chief and overall commander of the military affairs of the Two Guang.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the ninth year he rose to Right Censor-in-Chief and overall commander of Guang military affairs.

sentences.zh: 逾年乞歸，卒。

translations.literal: After more than a year he requested to return and died.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he asked to retire and died.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 孫祿，棲霞人。

translations.literal: Sun Lu, a native of Qixia.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Lu was from Qixia.

sentences.zh: 弘治九年進士。

translations.literal: Graduate of the jinshi degree in the ninth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in the ninth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 由戶部主事歷郎中。

translations.literal: From Ministry of Revenue principal clerk he passed through to director.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from a Revenue clerk to director.

sentences.zh: 瑾敗，起故官，累遷至應天府尹。

translations.literal: When Jin was defeated, he was raised from his former office and by cumulative promotion reached Metropolitan Prefect of Yingtian.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin's fall he was restored and eventually became prefect of Yingtian.

sentences.zh: 馬昊，本姓鄒，字宗大，寧夏人。

translations.literal: Ma Hao, original surname Zou, style name Zongda, a native of Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Hao, born Zou, styled Zongda, was from Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 弘治十二年進士。

translations.literal: Graduate of the jinshi degree in the twelfth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in the twelfth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 由行人選御史。

translations.literal: From courier he was selected as investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: He moved from the courier service to the censorate.

sentences.zh: 正德初，遷山東僉事，坐累謫真定推官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengde he was transferred to Shandong vice commissioner; sitting on accumulated guilt he was demoted to Zhending deputy magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhengde he became Shandong vice commissioner but soon was demoted to deputy magistrate of Zhending for an offense.

sentences.zh: 境內數有盜，昊教吏士習射，廣設方略，盜發輒獲。

translations.literal: Within the territory bandits appeared repeatedly; Hao taught clerks and gentry to practice archery, broadly laid out stratagems, and whenever bandits rose they were promptly seized.
translations.idiomatic: Banditry was frequent; Hao trained clerks and militia in archery, devised many tactics, and captured raiders whenever they struck.

sentences.zh: 再坐累謫判開州。

translations.literal: Again sitting on accumulated guilt he was demoted to assistant magistrate of Kaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted again to assistant magistrate of Kaizhou.

sentences.zh: 真定吏民伏闕請留，乃免。

translations.literal: The clerks and people of Zhending prostrated themselves at the gate to request he be kept; thereupon he was exempted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhending officials and commoners petitioned at court to keep him, and the demotion was revoked.

sentences.zh: 遷四川僉事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Sichuan vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Sichuan as vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 昊長身驍捷，善騎射，知兵。

translations.literal: Hao was tall in stature, valiant and agile, skilled at mounted archery, and knew warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Tall, agile, expert with bow and horse, he understood warfare.

sentences.zh: 巨寇方四、曹甫等方熾，洪鐘討之久無功。

translations.literal: The great bandits Fang Si, Cao Fu, and others were just then fierce; Hong Zhong campaigned against them for long without achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Great rebels Fang Si and Cao Fu were at their height; Hong Zhong's long campaign had failed.

sentences.zh: 昊至，閱所部，笑曰：「將不知兵，其何以戰？

translations.literal: When Hao arrived he reviewed those under his command and laughed, saying: "Generals who do not know warfare—how can they fight?"
translations.idiomatic: On arrival Hao inspected his troops and laughed: "How can generals who know nothing of war fight?"

sentences.zh: 」於是擇健卒千人分數隊，隊立長，教之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he chose a thousand sturdy soldiers, divided them into several squads, established a squad leader for each squad, and drilled them.
translations.idiomatic: He chose a thousand sturdy men, divided them into squads each with a leader, and trained them.

sentences.zh: 會甫將襲江津，昊從巡撫林俊剿賊，大敗之，俘斬及焚死者二千余人。

translations.literal: As Fu was about to strike Jiangjin, Hao followed Grand Coordinator Lin Jun to suppress the bandits and greatly defeated them; captives beheaded and those who died by fire totaled more than two thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu threatened Jiangjin, Hao joined grand coordinator Lin Jun, routed the rebels, and killed or captured more than two thousand.

sentences.zh: 明年，方四陷江津，破綦江，薄重慶。

translations.literal: The next year Fang Si took Jiangjin, broke Qijiang, and pressed close to Chongqing.
translations.idiomatic: Next year Fang Si took Jiangjin, stormed Qijiang, and threatened Chongqing.

sentences.zh: 昊夜出百騎，舉火擊賊，賊驚潰。

translations.literal: Hao by night sallied forth with a hundred horsemen, raised fires and struck the bandits; the bandits were startled and routed.
translations.idiomatic: Hao led a hundred horsemen out at night with torches, struck the camp, and rebels scattered in panic.

sentences.zh: 乘之，斬獲多，遂合羅、回土兵博賊。

translations.literal: Pressing the opportunity he beheaded and captured many; thereupon he united Luo and Hui native troops to grapple with the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed the pursuit, took many heads, and joined Luo and Hui tribal soldiers to finish the fight.

sentences.zh: 賊陳左而伏兵其右，昊以正兵當左，身率百騎搗其伏。

translations.literal: The bandits deployed their main force on the left while ambushing on the right; Hao used his regular troops to face the left and personally led a hundred horsemen to storm their ambush.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels held the left while ambushers waited on the right; Hao pinned the left with his main force and personally led a hundred cavalry against the ambush.

sentences.zh: 伏潰，趨左，左亦潰，四奔婺川，與甫相攻，眾遂散。

translations.literal: The ambush routed; he rushed toward the left; the left also routed; Si fled to Wuchuan and fought with Fu; the masses thereupon dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: The ambush broke; he wheeled on the left flank until it too collapsed; Si fled to Wuchuan, clashed with Fu, and the host dispersed.

sentences.zh: 四變姓名走，為他將所獲。

translations.literal: Si changed his name and fled and was seized by another general.
translations.idiomatic: Si fled under a false name and was caught by another commander.

sentences.zh: 昊再被獎，進副使，與總兵官楊宏擊敗甫。

translations.literal: Hao was again rewarded, advanced to vice commissioner, and with regional commander Yang Hong defeated Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Rewarded again, he was promoted to vice commissioner and with regional commander Yang Hong defeated Fu.

sentences.zh: 甫降，而其黨廖麻子並其眾，連陷銅梁、榮昌。

translations.literal: Fu surrendered, but his partisan Liao Mazhi combined their forces and in succession took Tongliang and Rongchang.
translations.idiomatic: Fu surrendered, but lieutenant Liao Mazhi rallied the remnants and seized Tongliang and Rongchang in succession.

sentences.zh: 坐奪冠帶。

translations.literal: For this he was punished by stripping his cap and belt.
translations.idiomatic: He was stripped of his official insignia for the setback.

sentences.zh: 時洪鐘已召還，巡撫高崇熙恇怯，復主撫。

translations.literal: At this time Hong Zhong had already been recalled; Grand Coordinator Gao Chongxi was timid and cowardly and again advocated pacification through appeasement.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Zhong had been recalled; grand coordinator Gao Chongxi was timid and again favored appeasement.

sentences.zh: 麻子等陽受約，崇熙遽罷諸軍，令副使張敏徙開縣臨江市民，空其地處之，許給復三年，為請於朝。

translations.literal: Mazhi and the others outwardly accepted treaties; Chongxi hastily dismissed all armies and ordered Vice Commissioner Zhang Min to relocate the populace of Linjiang market in Kaizhou, emptying the land to settle them there, promising restoration in three years, and requesting this of the court.
translations.idiomatic: Mazhi feigned agreement; Chongxi hastily disbanded the army and ordered vice commissioner Zhang Min to evacuate Linjiang townsfolk from Kaizhou and resettle them on empty land, with a three-year tax reprieve—petitioning the court for approval.

sentences.zh: 昊力爭，謂臨江市蜀襟喉，上達重、敘，下連湖、湘，地土饒衍，奈何棄以資賊，自遺患。

translations.literal: Hao strove to dispute it, saying: "Linjiang city is the throat of Shu; upward it reaches Chong and Xu; downward it connects Hu and Xiang; the land is rich and broad—why abandon it to supply bandits and leave calamity for oneself?"
translations.idiomatic: Hao argued fiercely: "Linjiang is the throat of Shu—linked upstream to Chongqing and Xuzhou, downstream to Hunan and Hubei, on fertile ground. Why surrender it to rebels and store up disaster?"

sentences.zh: 崇熙不從，昊乃益治兵觀變。

translations.literal: Chongxi did not follow; Hao thereupon all the more drilled troops and watched for changes.
translations.idiomatic: Chongxi refused; Hao redoubled military preparations and watched events.

sentences.zh: 其明年，賊果執敏叛。

translations.literal: The next year after that, the bandits indeed seized Min and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Next year the rebels duly seized Zhang Min and rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 詔逮崇熙，而擢昊右僉都御史代之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Chongxi seized, while Hao was promoted to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Chongxi was arrested by edict; Hao was promoted to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief in his place.

sentences.zh: 賊圍中江，將趨成都。

translations.literal: The bandits besieged Zhongjiang and were about to press toward Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels besieged Zhongjiang and marched toward Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 昊以五千騎與總督彭澤敗之。

translations.literal: Hao with five thousand horsemen and Grand Coordinator Peng Ze defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Hao and grand coordinator Peng Ze routed them with five thousand cavalry.

sentences.zh: 遊擊閻勛追斬麻子劍州，余眾走，推其黨喻思俸為主。

translations.literal: Guerrilla officer Yan Xun pursued and beheaded Mazhi at Jianzhou; the remaining masses fled and elevated his partisan Yu Sifeng as leader.
translations.idiomatic: Guerrilla officer Yan Xun pursued and killed Mazhi at Jianzhou; survivors fled and made lieutenant Yu Sifeng their chief.

sentences.zh: 總兵官陳珣追至富村，賊偽降。

translations.literal: Regional commander Chen Xun pursued to Fucun; the bandits feigned surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Regional commander Chen Xun chased them to Fucun, where they pretended to submit.

sentences.zh: 因北渡江，襲殺都指揮姚震，轉入巴山故巢。

translations.literal: Thereupon they crossed the river northward, ambushed and killed Regional Commander Yao Zhen, and turned into their old lair in Ba Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: They crossed the Yangtze north, ambushed and killed regional commander Yao Zhen, and withdrew to their old Ba Mountain lair.

sentences.zh: 尋出走大安鎮，珣不敢前。

translations.literal: Before long they went out and fled to Da'an Town; Xun did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they broke for Da'an Town; Xun would not advance.

sentences.zh: 而陜西兵與賊戰潰，賊遂越寧羌犯略陽。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Shaanxi troops fought the bandits and were routed; the bandits thereupon crossed Ningqiang and invaded Lüeyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi troops engaged them and collapsed; rebels crossed into Ningqiang and raided Lüeyang.

sentences.zh: 珣軍鼓噪，賊夜走，度廣元，為官軍所遏，還趨通、巴招余黨。

translations.literal: Xun's army beat drums and shouted; the bandits fled by night, crossed Guangyuan, were blocked by government troops, and returned pressing toward Tong and Ba to summon remaining partisans.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xun's men raised a tumult; rebels fled by night, were blocked at Guangyuan, and turned back toward Tongzhou and Bazhou to rally stragglers.

sentences.zh: 諸將率稱病不擊賊，詔逮珣，且讓昊。

translations.literal: The various generals for the most part claimed illness and would not strike the bandits; an edict ordered Xun seized and also reproached Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Most generals pleaded illness and refused to fight; Xun was arrested by edict and Hao was rebuked.

sentences.zh: 昊乃與彭澤督諸軍獲思俸西鄉山中，復與澤平內江賊駱松祥，群盜悉靖。

translations.literal: Hao then with Peng Ze supervised the various armies and captured Sifeng in the mountains of Xixiang; again with Ze he pacified the bandit Luo Songxiang of Neijiang; all roving bandits were entirely quieted.
translations.idiomatic: Hao and Peng Ze then took Sifeng in the Xixiang hills and crushed Neijiang rebel Luo Songxiang until every band was quiet.

sentences.zh: 錄功，進副都御史。

translations.literal: Merit was recorded; he was advanced to Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: For these exploits he was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 十年，亦不剌寇松藩，番人磨讓六少等乘機亂，為之向導，西土大震。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Ibars raided Songpan; the Tibetan Mo Rang Liushao and others seized the opportunity to rise in disorder and served as guides for them; the western territories were greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Ibars raided Songpan; Tibetans led by Mo Rang Liushao rose as guides, and the west was shaken.

sentences.zh: 昊招土番為間，發兵掩擊之。

translations.literal: Hao recruited native Tibetans as spies and sent troops to surprise and strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Hao enlisted tribal Tibetans as agents and launched a surprise attack.

sentences.zh: 千戶張倫等夜率熟番攻破賊，獲磨讓六少，亦不剌遁去。

translations.literal: Battalion commander Zhang Lun and others by night led familiar Tibetans to break the bandits, captured Mo Rang Liushao, and Ibars fled away.
translations.idiomatic: Battalion commander Zhang Lun led allied Tibetans in a night assault, captured Mo Rang Liushao, and Ibars escaped.

sentences.zh: 昊以松潘地險阻，番人往往邀劫饋運，乃督參將張傑等修築墻柵，自三舍堡至風洞關，凡五十里。

translations.literal: Hao, because Songpan's terrain was perilous and narrow and Tibetans often intercepted grain transports, thereupon supervised Assistant Commander Zhang Jie and others to build walls and palisades from Sanshe Fort to Fengdong Pass, altogether fifty li.
translations.idiomatic: Songpan's terrain invited ambush on supply lines, so Hao had assistant commander Zhang Jie build fifty li of wall from Sanshe Fort to Fengdong Pass.

sentences.zh: 賜敕褒之。

translations.literal: An imperial letter of praise was bestowed upon him.
translations.idiomatic: The throne sent a patent of commendation.

sentences.zh: 烏蒙、芒部二府壤接筠連、珙縣，圍亙千里，山箐深阻。

translations.literal: The two prefectures of Wumeng and Mangbu had territories adjoining Junlian and Gong counties; the circumference spanned a thousand li; mountain ravines were deep and obstructive.
translations.idiomatic: Wumeng and Mangbu adjoined Junlian and Gong across a thousand li of deep mountain ravines.

sentences.zh: 諸蠻僰人子、羿子、仲家子、苗子、倮、佫等雜居其中。

translations.literal: Various southern barbarians—Bo, Yi, Zhongjia, Miao, Luo, Gelao, and the like—lived mixed among them.
translations.idiomatic: Bo, Yi, Zhongjia, Miao, Luo, Gelao, and other tribes lived intermingled there.

sentences.zh: 有僰人子普法惡者，通漢語，曉符錄。

translations.literal: There was a Bo tribesman named Pufa'e who understood Han speech and knew talismans and registers.
translations.idiomatic: A Bo tribesman named Pufa'e spoke Chinese and knew ritual talismans.

sentences.zh: 妄言彌勒出世，自稱蠻王，煽諸夷作亂。

translations.literal: He falsely claimed Maitreya was born into the world, styled himself Barbarian King, and incited the various Yi to rise in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed the coming of Maitreya, styled himself Barbarian King, and stirred the tribes to revolt.

sentences.zh: 流民謝文禮、謝文義應之。

translations.literal: Vagrant commoners Xie Wenli and Xie Wenyi responded to him.
translations.idiomatic: Vagabonds Xie Wenli and Xie Wenyi joined him.

sentences.zh: 都指揮杜琮戰敗，文義奪其胄。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Du Cong was defeated in battle; Wenyi seized his helmet.
translations.idiomatic: Regional commander Du Cong was defeated and Wenyi took his helmet.

sentences.zh: 十二年，昊督指揮曹昱進討，法惡敗，走保青山寨。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Hao supervised Commander Cao Yu to advance and campaign; Fa'e was defeated and fled to hold Green Mountain Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Hao led commander Cao Yu against him; Pufa'e was beaten back to Green Mountain Fort.

sentences.zh: 昊分據水口，絕其汲道，闕南方圍待之。

translations.literal: Hao divided forces to hold the water mouth, cut off their water-drawing route, left the south open, and encircled waiting for them.
translations.idiomatic: Hao seized the water source, cut supply, left the south open as bait, and waited in siege.

sentences.zh: 賊乏水渴，突南圍，官軍遮擊。

translations.literal: The bandits lacked water and were thirsty; they burst through the southern encirclement; government troops intercepted and struck.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels, parched, charged the southern gap; government troops intercepted them.

sentences.zh: 法惡中流矢死，諸蠻大奔。

translations.literal: Fa'e was struck by a flying arrow and died; all the barbarians fled in great rout.
translations.idiomatic: Pufa'e fell to an arrow; the tribes scattered in rout.

sentences.zh: 以功，再進右都御史，蔭子錦衣世百戶。

translations.literal: For merit he was again advanced to Right Censor-in-Chief; his son was ennobled as hereditary battalion commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard for a hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was again made Right Censor-in-Chief and his son ennobled as hereditary Embroidered Guard commander for a hundred households.

sentences.zh: 昊有才氣，能應變，揮霍自喜，所向輒有功。

translations.literal: Hao had talent and spirit, could respond to change, was freehanded and pleased with himself, and wherever he turned there was achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Talented and resourceful, spendthrift and self-satisfied, he won wherever he was sent.

sentences.zh: 然官川中久，狎其俗，銳意立功名，卒以是敗。

translations.literal: Yet having served long in office in Sichuan he was intimate with local customs, keen to establish fame and merit, and in the end failed because of this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet long service in Sichuan had made him too familiar with local ways and too hungry for glory—and that ruined him.

sentences.zh: 先是，亦不剌既遁，昊移兵攻小東路番寨未下，茂州群蠻懼見侵，遂糾生苗圍城堡。

translations.literal: Previously, after Ibars had already fled, Hao shifted troops to attack the small eastern route Tibetan stockades without taking them; the various barbarians of Maozhou feared they would be invaded and thereupon rallied living Miao to besiege the forts.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Ibars's escape, Hao attacked eastern-route Tibetan camps without success; Maozhou tribes feared invasion and rallied Miao allies to besiege government forts.

sentences.zh: 參將芮錫等討之，兵敗，指揮龐昇等皆死。

translations.literal: Assistant Commander Rui Xi and others campaigned against them; the army was defeated; Commander Pang Sheng and others all died.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant commander Rui Xi's counterattack failed; commander Pang Sheng and others were killed.

sentences.zh: 又嘗遣副總兵張傑、副使吳澧擊松潘南北二路番，不利，亡軍士三千余人，匿不以聞。

translations.literal: He also once sent Deputy Regional Commander Zhang Jie and Vice Commissioner Wu Li to strike the northern and southern routes of Songpan Tibetans; it was not advantageous; more than three thousand soldiers were lost; he concealed it and did not report.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent deputy commander Zhang Jie and vice commissioner Wu Li against northern and southern Songpan Tibetans; they lost more than three thousand men—losses he concealed.

sentences.zh: 僰蠻平，不置戍守，遽班師。

translations.literal: When the Bo barbarians were pacified he did not set garrisons but hastily withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: After the Bo revolt he withdrew without leaving garrisons.

sentences.zh: 請改高縣為州，設長吏，增高、珙、筠連田租千八百石，令指揮魏武度田奪降人業給之軍民。

translations.literal: He requested to change Gaoxian into a prefecture, establish a chief official, raise the land tax of Gao, Gong, and Junlian by eighteen hundred shi, and order Commander Wei Wu to survey fields and seize surrendered people's holdings to grant to troops and commoners.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed elevating Gaoxian to a prefecture, appointing a chief magistrate, raising rents in Gao, Gong, and Junlian by eighteen hundred shi, and ordering commander Wei Wu to survey fields and distribute surrendered lands to troops and settlers.

sentences.zh: 而珙縣知縣步梁窺昊意，誘殺降人阿尚。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the magistrate of Gong county Bu Liang spied Hao's intent and enticed and killed the surrendered tribesman A Shang.
translations.idiomatic: Gong magistrate Bu Liang, reading Hao's mind, lured and killed the surrendered tribesman A Shang.

sentences.zh: 杜琮以亡胄故，怨文義，潛使人購其頭。

translations.literal: Du Cong, because of the lost helmet, bore resentment against Wenyi and secretly sent men to purchase his head.
translations.idiomatic: Du Cong, still angry over his stolen helmet, secretly offered a price for Wenyi's head.

sentences.zh: 於是文義乘群蠻怨，嗾之，遂大訌。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wen Yi, taking advantage of the tribes' resentment, incited them, and a great uprising followed.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Wen Yi, seizing on the tribes' resentment, incited them, and a great uprising broke out.

sentences.zh: 攻高、慶符二縣，破其城。

translations.literal: They attacked the two counties of Gao and Qingfu and stormed their cities.
translations.idiomatic: They attacked Gao and Qingfu counties and stormed their cities.

sentences.zh: 琮率兵禦之，又敗，死傷七百人。

translations.literal: Du Cong led troops to resist them but was again defeated, with seven hundred dead and wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Du Cong led troops to resist them but was defeated again, with seven hundred dead and wounded.

sentences.zh: 自黎雅以西，天全六番皆相繼亂。

translations.literal: From Liya westward, the six tribes of Tianquan all rose in disorder in succession.
translations.idiomatic: From Liya westward, the six tribes of Tianquan all rose in disorder one after another.

sentences.zh: 南京給事中孫懋暨巡按御史盧雍、黎龍先後劾昊。

translations.literal: Nanjing supervising secretary Sun Mao and touring censors Lu Yong and Li Long impeached Hao in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing supervising secretary Sun Mao and touring censors Lu Yong and Li Long impeached Hao in succession.

sentences.zh: 十四年遂遣官逮昊。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year officials were dispatched to arrest Hao.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year officials were dispatched to arrest Hao.

sentences.zh: 行至河南，疏稱疾篤，留於家。

translations.literal: When he reached Henan he memorialized that his illness was grave and was left at home.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Henan he memorialized that his illness was grave and was allowed to remain at home.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，始就逮，尋削籍歸。

translations.literal: When Shizong took the throne he was at last taken into custody, and soon was struck from the rolls and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong took the throne he was at last taken into custody, and soon was struck from the rolls and sent home.

sentences.zh: 楊一清、胡世寧薦之，為桂萼所駁而止。

translations.literal: Yang Yiqing and Hu Shining recommended him, but Gui E refuted this and the matter stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yiqing and Hu Shining recommended him, but Gui E objected and the matter went no further.

sentences.zh: 久之，卒。

translations.literal: After a long while he died.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he died.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：何鑒綰中樞，能任諸將滅賊，蓋其時楊廷和在政府，閣部同心，故克奏效雲爾。

translations.literal: The appraiser says: He Jian held the central command and was able to entrust the generals to destroy the bandits—this was because at that time Yang Tinghe was in the government and the court and ministries were of one mind; therefore they could achieve effect thus.
translations.idiomatic: The appraiser says: He Jian held the central command and was able to entrust his generals to destroy the bandits—largely because Yang Tinghe was then in government and the court and ministries acted as one; that is how success was won.

sentences.zh: 馬中錫雅負時望，而軍旅非其所長，適用取敗。

translations.literal: Ma Zhongxi bore fine repute in his time, but military affairs were not his strength; employed inappropriately he met defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zhongxi bore fine repute in his day, but military affairs were not his strength; put to the wrong use, he met defeat.

sentences.zh: 然觀劉宸阻降之言，亦可以觀朝事矣。

translations.literal: Yet in viewing Liu Chen's words blocking surrender one may also view the affairs of the court.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Liu Chen's words refusing surrender also reveal much about the state of the court.

sentences.zh: 陸完交結之罪浮於首功，得從八議，有佚罰焉。

translations.literal: Lu Wan's crime of forming illicit connections outweighed his chief merit; he was allowed the Eight Mitigations—there was leniency in his punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Wan's crime of forming illicit connections outweighed his chief merit; he was allowed the benefit of the Eight Mitigations—his punishment was lenient.

sentences.zh: 洪鐘、陳金威略甚著，而土兵之謠，聞之心惻，斯又統戎旃者所當留意也。

translations.literal: Hong Zhong and Chen Jin were very distinguished in martial strategy, yet the ballad of the native troops—hearing it the heart is moved to pity; this too is what those who command armies ought to heed.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Zhong and Chen Jin were highly distinguished in martial strategy, yet the ballad of the native troops moves the heart to pity on hearing it—this too is what those who command armies ought to bear in mind.
